title: [Reshard] Add model-weight Transfer Engine adapters
body:
## Description

This PR adds model-weight adapters that execute validated reshard plans through
Mooncake Transfer Engine.

The adapters consume an attested `TransferPlan`, fresh runtime binding
manifests, and framework-provided allocation guards. They validate the selected
runtime fragments, lower compact N-D transfer regions into bounded TE batches,
and execute either target-initiated reads or source-initiated writes. The
resource-neutral TE executor remains independent of model names and framework
tensor layouts.

The execution lifecycle is fail-closed. GPU allocations and memory
registrations remain pinned until completion reaches a known terminal state.
Unknown completion or cleanup outcomes are retained by the pending-transfer
manager, fence further submissions on the same engine, and expose a pending ID
for status and recovery handling. Reader and sink paths share the same
completion, registration, allocation-lifetime, and operation-budget contracts.

This PR also documents the execution boundary and public APIs. Store
persistence, framework runtime discovery, model-specific conversion, and
quantization or packed-layout transformation remain separate layers.

Related RFC: #3111

title: [TransferEngine] Make the RDMA worker idle spin window configurable
body:
## Description

`WorkerPool::transferWorker` busy-polls for a hard-coded 100 ms (`kWaitPeriodInNano`) after its device instance becomes idle, and only then parks on the pool's condition variable. The idle check is pool-wide (`processed_slice_count_ == submitted_slice_count_`). As a result, every worker of an instance keeps polling while any slice on that instance is in flight, and each polling worker occupies a whole CPU core.

When transfers arrive more often than every 100 ms but are far from saturating the NICs, the workers never park. We hit this in a PD-disaggregated deployment. An 8-GPU decode node pulled KV cache over 8 HCAs with `MC_WORKERS_PER_CTX=4`, which is 256 workers across 8 processes. Those workers kept about 90 cores busy, although the actual post and poll work needed only a small fraction of that. The node exceeded its container CPU quota, and CFS throttling then stalled the inference processes.

This PR adds `MC_RDMA_WORKER_IDLE_SPIN_US` to set the window:

- The default is `100000` (100 ms), so behavior is unchanged unless the variable is set.
- The range is `0`-`10000000`. `0` parks a worker as soon as its instance is idle.
- Parsing is strict, as with `MC_CONN_PAUSE_TTL_MS`. Non-numeric, negative, out-of-range or suffixed values are ignored with a WARNING and the default is kept. An accepted value is logged at INFO.
- The parking protocol is unchanged: the double check under `cond_mutex_`, the `notify_all` from submitters while `parked_worker_count_ > 0`, and the 1 s `wait_for` backstop. A worker with outstanding completions still polls.
- The UB transport (`ub_context.cpp`) has the same constant but a different idle loop, and is left unchanged.

Trade-off: with a shorter window, a parked worker pays a thread wake-up when the next transfer arrives. Deployments that care most about latency and have spare cores can keep the default.

title: [TransferEngine] Add opt-in strict dest-device affinity for rail-isolated NICs
body:
## Description

On rail-isolated RDMA fabrics, a local HCA cannot reach a different-name peer HCA. The existing path pins one local device for a whole request and treats same-name pairing as a preference: if that peer is missing, it falls back to another device. That fallback shows up as retry exceeded / `IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR` (see #35 and #1450).

This adds an opt-in switch, `MC_ENABLE_STRICT_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY`. It defaults to off, so full-mesh mlx5 and the soft `MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY` preference are unchanged.

When the switch is on:

1. Each slice picks its own local HCA instead of pinning one HCA for the whole request.
2. The peer HCA must have the same name. There is no fallback, including when the matched rail is paused.
3. `retry_count == 0` round-robins `preferred_hca` and `avail_hca` together, so every listed rail can be used.

It is mutually exclusive with `MC_ENABLE_HCA_PEER_AFFINITY`. If both are set, peer selection falls back to the default.

title: [TransferEngine] Clamp RD-atomic QP depths to the device capability
body:
## Description

Fixes #4309. The RTR transition hard-coded `max_dest_rd_atomic = 16` and the RTS transition hard-coded `max_rd_atomic = 16`. Some RNICs advertise fewer, so `ibv_modify_qp()` returns an error and the endpoint never reaches RTS.

Reuse the device-capability clamping already performed by `updateGlobalConfig()`: cache `max_qp_init_rd_atom` / `max_qp_rd_atom` in `GlobalConfig`, lower them to the values reported by `ibv_query_device()`, and apply them when building the QP attributes. This is the same pattern already used for `max_wr`, `max_sge`, `max_cqe`, etc.

title: [TransferEngine] Pipeline CUDA TCP staging with pinned buffers
body:
## Description

Use CUDA pinned host buffers for TCP staging and prefetch the next device-to-host chunk while the socket sends the current chunk. The two buffers are reused within a session; non-CUDA device backends retain their existing staging path. This is a focused part of the TCP fallback work in #3446.

On one RTX 5090 using same-host TCP loopback, 16 MiB transfers with 64 KiB chunks (30 iterations per run, three runs) had median WRITE throughput of 2536.88 to 3771.82 MiB/s (+48.7%) and READ throughput of 2538.43 to 3808.08 MiB/s (+50.0%). Cross-host performance has not been measured.

title: [Bugfix][TransferEngine] Stage TCP CUDA copies off the legacy stream
body:
## Description

With the CUDA build, the TCP transport staged device memory through a synchronous `cudaMemcpy` on the legacy default stream, so any transfer of GPU buffers waited behind every kernel the process already had queued — the reporter sees streamed tokens reaching the client two at a time. The `USE_MACA` build already went through `copyTcpCudaMemory` (a private non-blocking stream, `cudaMemcpyAsync`, then a sync of that stream); the CUDA build didn't.

This lifts `copyTcpCudaMemory` out of the `USE_MACA` guard so every GPU build has it, and routes all four staging sites (`ServerSession`/`ClientSession` x `readBody`/`writeBody`) through it. The trailing stream sync keeps the copy's completion contract identical for callers.

Neighbor note: #4233 pipelines CUDA TCP staging with pinned buffers but deliberately keeps `cudaStreamDefault` (legacy-stream semantics) for its session stream, so the stall this fixes survives that PR. The two are complementary; whichever lands second rebases.

Fixes #4323

title: [Store] Bridge BatchGet completion into CUDA graph waits
body:
## Description

Add a CUDA-only completion barrier that lets a captured graph wait for a Store `TransferFuture` or a background `Client::BatchGet`. The barrier uses a mapped pinned host flag and `cuStreamWaitValue32`; it can be rearmed after each replay. `StartBatchGetWithCudaBarrier` retains the existing replica selection and read lease path. A failed read still releases the graph wait, and callers must discard graph output unless `barrier->wait()` returns `ErrorCode::OK`.

This is an incremental piece of #3610. It does not route the user's stream through Store transports, add `RealClient`/`PyClient` `*_on_stream` APIs, or cover Ascend/ADXL.

title: [Bugfix] Reconnect idle TCP lanes after peer close
body:
## Description

Before reusing an idle TCP lane, peek at its socket to detect a peer that has closed the connection. On EOF or socket error, discard the stale socket and allow the lane to reconnect on the next pump round. This addresses a peer-close failure mode related to #4209; the issue's original vLLM/H20 deployment and its suspected stale CLOSED group were not reproduced here.

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Recover SHM backing paths during basic registration
body:
## Description

With only SHM enabled, `allocateLocalMemory(&ptr, size)` followed by `registerLocalMemory(ptr, size)` succeeds, but a peer's READ/WRITE fails because the buffer is never advertised for SHM. The basic allocation overload discards its temporary `MemoryOptions`, and basic registration supplies fresh options without the backing path. The native Python basic APIs have the same failure.

When no explicit path is provided, recover it from SHM's existing allocation map under its existing mutex. Explicit paths keep their behavior; unrelated allocations remain unregistered for SHM. This changes only registration, with no new state or transfer-path mechanism.

This follows #4250: allocation now succeeds, but the basic registration path still loses the backing name. The regression covers scalar/vector registration and READ/WRITE payloads between two SHM-only engines. It is separate from #3581's remote relocation-cache issue.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## How Has This Been Tested?

Fresh Linux CPU-only build from main `16b7ba3c7364eb8d36d04378bc7d28013bea1a1e`, with `WITH_TE=ON`, `USE_TENT=ON`, `BUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON`, `USE_CUDA=OFF`.

```bash
cmake --build build --target tent_local_memory_lifecycle_test tent_shm_transport_test tentpy -j4
ctest --test-dir build -R '^tent_(local_memory_lifecycle|shm_transport|python_guards)_test$' --output-on-failure
pre-commit run --files mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/src/transport/shm/shm_transport.cpp mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/tests/local_memory_lifecycle_test.cpp
```

- [x] Integration tests pass: two-engine SHM READ/WRITE and payload checks in the new regression.

title: [Bugfix][CI/Build] Reject ROCm wheels without multi-protocol routing
body:
## Description

Prevent ROCm release artifacts from silently shipping without the multi-protocol routing required for combined RDMA and HIP segments.

The published `mooncake-transfer-engine-rocm==0.3.13.post1` CPython 3.10 wheel was built from `v0.3.13.post1` (`719735896c86b56fabec6cf3e825fb2ea640597a`). Its release workflow enabled HIP but omitted `-DENABLE_MULTI_PROTOCOL=ON`, while that CMake option defaults to `OFF`. In a reported two-node MI355X test using `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`, a cross-host GPU WRITE selected HIP IPC and failed with `hipIpcOpenMemHandle: invalid device context`. Rebuilding the same source with multi-protocol support enabled passed 16 bidirectional 2 MiB GPU WRITEs with full source and destination byte-integrity checks.

PR #3338 already corrected the current ROCm CI and release configuration to pass `-DENABLE_MULTI_PROTOCOL=ON`. This PR adds the missing artifact-level guard so a future workflow/configuration regression cannot publish another incorrectly configured ROCm wheel:

- expose `mooncake.engine.SUPPORT_MULTI_PROTOCOL` from the compiled extension;
- require ROCm wheel verification to reject an explicitly disabled capability;
- retain a narrow binary-marker fallback for workflow-dispatch backfills of older tags that predate the Python capability attribute;
- add positive and deliberately broken negative unit tests, including a chunk-boundary marker test.

Independent artifact inspection reproduced the build mismatch:

- affected PyPI CPython 3.10 wheel SHA-256: `4263d8a48c8bd05a340c19fa7533e012a3d4b9ac284161142a3062c24a4de4c6`; its `engine.so` lacks the multi-protocol-only `MC_DISABLE_HIP` marker and is rejected by this guard;
- current-main CI artifact from run `34701684601`, head `6ae74b3512c4d0ce70c4a7c22bc4f33aeb7d3ff8`, SHA-256 `084de7e711884f0fe9602ad0d5de0b46589526655e5a7c8b71ac8f53f616fe7a`; its `engine.so` contains the marker and is accepted.

This PR prevents recurrence but does not replace the immutable PyPI `0.3.13.post1` files. A new ROCm package version is still required to make the corrected build available through normal `pip install`.

Related: #3108, #3338. Open PR #3970 also edits the verifier, and #4177 moves the E2E verifier path; this change is intentionally narrow and may need to be carried across whichever layout lands first.

title: [Store/RDMA] Fix ibv_reg_mr failures with 2MB hugepage SHM (memfd + MTT alignment)
body:
## Description

When `MC_STORE_USE_HUGEPAGE=1` is set, starting the Mooncake store with a large KV cache buffer causes `ibv_reg_mr` to fail with **EINVAL (-600)**, preventing RDMA registration of the host memory pool.

Observed on **GLM-5.2-FP8, TP=8**: each TP worker allocates four ShmHelper pools totalling ~11–12 GB per worker (~90 GB across 8 workers). Representative pool sizes (one worker, 2 MB hugepages; the physical segment is what `ShmHelper::allocate()` actually maps, rounded up to hugepage granularity):

| Pool | Requested size | Physical segment (hugepage-rounded) | Rounding overhead |
|------|---------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------|
| swa | 3,779,571,220 B (3,604.5 MB) | 3,781,165,056 B (1,803 × 2 MB) | +1.5 MB |
| deepseek_v4_c4 | 4,434,553,733 B (4,229.9 MB) | 4,435,476,480 B (2,115 × 2 MB) | +0.9 MB |
| indexer | 998,579,896 B (952.3 MB) | 1,000,341,504 B (477 × 2 MB) | +1.7 MB |
| state | 773,094,113 B (737.3 MB) | 773,849,088 B (369 × 2 MB) | +0.7 MB |

None of the four requested sizes is a 2 MB multiple, so every pool carries the hazard below; the two largest surfaced first: `swa` (3,604 MB, registered with its logical size, whose end lands inside the last huge page of the mapping) and `deepseek_v4_c4` (4,230 MB, above the 4 GiB threshold where the parallel preTouch path trial-registers each thread's block).

The rounding overhead itself is negligible (≤ 2 MB per pool, ~5 MB per worker, ~40 MB across 8 workers) and — importantly — **this PR does not change allocation at all**: `ShmHelper` already rounds the mapping up to hugepage granularity. The fix is to make registration agree with the mapping instead of reshaping the mapping to fit the registration.

### Root cause

strace-level tracing pinpointed the failure origin, and it never reaches the mlx5 driver. After `ibv_fork_init()` is enabled, every `ibv_reg_mr` first runs `ibv_dontfork_range()`, which issues `madvise(MADV_DONTFORK)` over the memory range. The kernel refuses to split a hugetlb VMA at a non-hugepage-aligned boundary, so any registered range whose start or end falls inside a huge page fails with **EINVAL** — before the driver is ever reached. For 2 MB hugepages this means every registered range must start and end on 2 MB boundaries (and for 1 GB hugepages, on 1 GB boundaries).

This requirement is violated at two points in the call chain, both of which must be fixed:

### Bug 1: register_buffer passes the logical size (`real_client.cpp`)

`register_buffer()` is called from Python with the original requested size (`tensor.nbytes`), which is not a huge-page multiple. Because `ShmHelper::allocate()` rounds the physical mapping up to hugepage granularity, the registered range ends inside the last huge page of the mapping — exactly where the kernel refuses to split the VMA.

### Bug 2: preTouch splits large buffers into fixed 4 KB blocks (`memory_location.cpp` / `rdma_transport.cpp`)

For buffers ≥ 4 GiB, `preTouchMemory()` splits the buffer into per-thread blocks (`length / num_threads`, 4 KB granular) and trial-registers each block on the RDMA path. Any block boundary that is not hugepage-aligned triggers the same EINVAL, even when the buffer as a whole is properly aligned.

Bug 1 controls what length is registered; Bug 2 controls the intermediate ranges touched during preTouch. Both must respect hugepage boundaries, and both must agree with the physical mapping produced by `ShmHelper`.

### Testing

- New end-to-end suite `real_client_hugepage_register_test` (4 tests, real client + in-proc master, `MC_STORE_USE_HUGEPAGE=1`). Run with `PROTOCOL=rdma DEVICE_NAME=mlx5_0` for full discriminating power:

  | Test | Discriminating input | Unfixed | Fixed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | SegmentBaseRegistersFullSegment | 8MB segment, base registered with logical size 3MB+512 | EINVAL on rdma | succeeds (widened to 8MB) |
  | PreTouchPageAlignedBlocksOnLargeSegment | 4GiB+1MB → 2049-page segment, not divisible by 8/16 threads | preTouch trial-registration EINVAL | succeeds with page-aligned blocks |
  | HotCacheShmRegistersAlignedSegment | 33MB cache / 3MB blocks (not a 2MB multiple) | hot cache silently disabled (EINVAL) | `IsHotCacheEnabled()` true |
  | MisalignedInteriorSubRangeRegistersExactly | interior ptr base+1MB, len 3MB+512 | EINVAL | still fails on rdma (by design); succeeds on tcp |

  Note: the last test intentionally stays last — a deliberately failed `ibv_reg_mr` leaves residue in libibverbs' process-global fork-protection bookkeeping (rdma-core does not roll back DONTFORK on failure), which can poison the next registration in the same process.
- `client_local_hot_cache_test` extended with 4 block-bookkeeping cases (39 total).
- Full-store verification on an mlx5_0 host: 4098 MB and 24.3 GB buffers now register reliably (80/80 passes). Suite results: hugepage suite 4/4 PASSED (rdma), hot cache suite 39/39 PASSED.

```bash
cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DUSE_RDMA=ON \
      -DUSE_HTTP=ON -DWITH_STORE=ON -DUSE_NVMEOF=OFF -DUSE_SPDK=OFF
cmake --build build --target real_client_hugepage_register_test \
      client_local_hot_cache_test --parallel 32
PROTOCOL=rdma DEVICE_NAME=mlx5_0 \
  ./build/mooncake-store/tests/real_client_hugepage_register_test
./build/mooncake-store/tests/client_local_hot_cache_test
```

Requires `vm.nr_hugepages > 0` (the suite SKIPs otherwise). Pass criterion: gtest prints `[  PASSED  ] N tests.`; the widening is also directly visible in the log line `Registering HugeTLB shared-memory segment: base=…, segment_size=…, logical_size=…`.

title: [Bugfix][Python] Use the buffer byte length instead of the element count in put and upsert
body:
## Description

`put`, `upsert`, `put_batch` and `upsert_batch` in `mooncake-integration/store/store_py.cpp` built their value span from `py::buffer_info::size`. In pybind11 that is the number of elements, not bytes, so any non-byte buffer (a numpy `float32` array, `array.array("f")`, a multi-byte `memoryview`) was silently truncated to one byte per element while the call still returned `0`. Strides were also ignored, so a non-contiguous view stored the wrong bytes. `put_parts` and `upsert_parts` already guarded against this; the four functions above did not.

This PR adds one helper, `contiguous_buffer_span`, that returns `size * itemsize` bytes and raises `ValueError` for a strided buffer, and uses it in the four bindings. The check runs before the GIL is released. Byte inputs behave exactly as before; contiguous typed buffers now store their full contents; strided views are rejected instead of being mis-stored. `put_parts` / `upsert_parts` are unchanged.

Fixes #4299

title: [Store] Add Intel XPU host-staging path to the Store client, Python e2e and vLLM-XPU smoke tests
body:
## Description

This is **PR3** of the Intel XPU enablement series (RFC #4031; PR1 #4030 added
the TENT XPU platform, PR2 #4157 added the XPU transport, routing and
host-staging in the Transfer Engine). It brings the Mooncake Store client up on
Intel XPU and adds end-to-end acceptance tests against an unmodified vLLM-XPU.

**Store**
- `mooncake-store/src/device/xpu_accelerator_device.cpp` (new, built only under
  `USE_XPU`): a SYCL-backed `AcceleratorDevice` (vendor `kIntel`). It
  classifies any USM pointer against the platform default context (the one
  PyTorch allocates from), so foreign device memory is recognised; copies run
  on queues bound to that context; pinned host memory comes from
  `sycl::malloc_host`. Linked in through `EnsureXpuAcceleratorDeviceLinked()`.
- `accelerator_device.h` / `accelerator_registry.cpp`: `kIntel` vendor and the
  registration hook.
- `mooncake-store/src/CMakeLists.txt`: add the source and a `USE_XPU` branch in
  the D2H-staging block.

**icpx compile fixes** (behaviour-neutral for GCC)
- vendored `fmt` 8.0.1 `core.h`: two upstream-equivalent fixes so the
  `consteval` `FMT_STRING` checks compile under clang-based compilers.
- `client_service.cpp`: define `Client::BatchUpsert` after `PutOperation` is
  complete (`std::vector<PutOperation>` was instantiated on an incomplete type).

**Engine selection is unchanged** (per review on #4157): Intel XPU is only
supported by the TENT engine, so XPU deployments must set `MC_USE_TENT=1`. The
smoke scripts default it via `os.environ.setdefault`, the Python XPU test skips
unless it is set, and the `MC_USE_TENT` row in the store deployment guide notes
the requirement.

**Tests**
- `pybind_client_test`: `XpuDeviceBufferPutGetRoundTrips` (`put_from` /
  `get_into` on `sycl::malloc_device` buffers, byte-equal), compiled with
  `MOONCAKE_TEST_XPU_H2D` under `USE_XPU`.
- `mooncake-wheel/tests/test_put_get_tensor.py`: `test_xpu_local_copy_paths`
  (`put_tensor` / `upsert_tensor` from `device="xpu"`, `get_tensor_into_cuda`
  into a registered XPU tensor, 4 MiB `put_from` / `get_into` round trip). The
  class now closes the store in `tearDownClass`: leaving it to the process-exit
  backstop tears the client down from a C `atexit` handler after the
  interpreter and the SYCL runtime have finalized, which on XPU intermittently
  aborted in `free()` while joining the client's worker threads.
- `scripts/xpu/vllm_store_smoke.py`: one vLLM instance on an Intel XPU with
  vLLM's V1 `MooncakeStoreConnector` (`kv_role=kv_both`) and local prefix
  caching disabled. Request 1 prefills and the connector saves the KV blocks
  into Mooncake Store (XPU KV cache → host staging → segment); request 2 is
  identical, cannot hit vLLM's own prefix cache, so the connector loads the
  blocks back into the XPU KV cache and decode resumes from them. PASS requires
  identical non-empty greedy tokens and connector metrics showing
  `save_put` / `load_get` keys with zero failures.
- `scripts/xpu/vllm_store_pd_smoke.py`: a vLLM `kv_producer` on one XPU
  (embedded Mooncake segment + master) and a `kv_consumer` on another
  (standalone-store, no segment), so every decode-side load is a real
  cross-device pull from the prefill segment. `--role local` spawns both on one
  node with `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:{0,1}`; `--role prefill` /
  `--role decode` run the halves on separate nodes.
- Both scripts carry two in-process shims for vLLM ≤ 0.29 code that is
  CUDA-specific rather than Mooncake-specific, to be dropped once fixed
  upstream: the connector's `wait_for_save` uses `torch.cuda.Event` (a raising
  dummy on XPU torch → aliased to `torch.xpu.Event`), and
  `ChunkedTokenDatabase.prepare_values` computes KV addresses in `np.int64`,
  which overflows on Level Zero USM pointers (≥ 2^63) → `uint64` math (the
  Mooncake bindings already take `uintptr_t`). Because of the shims the engine
  core runs in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`).

title: [3/3] [Store] Avoid staging for remote GPU reads
body:
## Description

Avoid mandatory CPU staging when the selected remote memory replica can be
read directly into a GPU destination through Transfer Engine.

## Stack

This is **[3/3]** of the RFC implementation stack:

1. #2966 — HOST_NUMA/Fabric Transfer Engine prerequisite (merged).
2. #3335 — Provider-owned EGM Store pool.
3. #3431 — direct remote-memory reads into GPU destinations (this PR).

The head branch is a strict child of #3335. With #2966 merged, GitHub now
shows the two remaining Store commits against `main`. The logical review
increment for this PR is still the four-file direct-read change. It will be
rebased onto `main` after #3335 merges.

## Problem

Remote memory reads into GPU buffers fall back to CPU staging even when
Transfer Engine can write directly to the destination. Direct-read eligibility
must follow the selected replica's transport, which can differ from the
protocol requested at client setup.

The staging path adds a CPU allocation and host-to-device copy, which can
become the throughput bottleneck for cross-node paths such as EGM to HBM.

## Fix

The private direct-read predicate now receives the selected
`Replica::Descriptor` and uses the memory replica's actual
`buffer_descriptor.protocol_`:

| Selected replica | Destination behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `nvlink` | Ordinary CUDA destination is passed directly to Transfer Engine |
| `rdma` | Direct only when the full destination range is Store-registered |
| Other protocols | Existing CPU staging fallback |

The affected full, ranged, and batched GPU-read paths pass the selected replica.
The newer snapshot APIs retain their existing registration and lease contracts.
There is no new Transfer Engine introspection API, public C++/Python API, wire
schema, or configuration change.

## Relationship to existing work

- #3197 removed staging for same-process GPU reads but intentionally retained
  the remote path.
- RFC #2479 proposes broader zero-copy read/write work. This PR only fixes the
  remote memory-read decision and does not add the broader lifecycle changes.
- RFC #2914 and #3335 expose the performance impact through cross-node
  EGM-to-HBM reads.

## Review size

- 1 logical commit.
- 4 changed files.
- +98/-6 lines relative to #3335.

## Validation

The direct-read logic and tests are unchanged. This update replays the patch
onto the updated EGM Store implementation in #3335; only the header insertion
context changes alongside its new private setup overload.

- [x] clang-format 20 check on PR-changed C/C++ lines.
- [x] `git diff --check` and all applicable PR-scoped hooks, including CMake formatting.
- [x] CUDA-on and CUDA-off direct-read regression tests (3 entries each).
- [x] CUDA-on VMM regression tests (2 entries).
- [x] CUDA-on/off EGM configuration/capacity and backend-selection regressions.
- [x] CUDA-off Transfer Engine, Store, Master and Python binding build.
- [x] CPU/TCP tensor snapshot: 3/3 with no skips; probe exports and close/fresh-setup smoke.
- [x] New-head strict Sphinx documentation build.
- [x] New-head complete `unit-tests` sweep (233/233) and GitHub Actions CI Gate.

The previous revision's green checks are not evidence for this update.
The full CTest sweep (233/233), strict Sphinx build and CI Gate have passed
for this revision.
The earlier upstream CMake formatting issue is fixed in the new base; no hook
exception is needed. Repository-wide `pre-commit run --all-files` is not a merge gate.

The regression matrix intentionally crosses requested and selected protocols:

- requested `nvlink` + selected RDMA replica: staging until the full
  destination range is registered;
- requested `rdma` + selected NVLink replica: direct GPU destination;
- TCP/other replica: staging fallback;
- registered-range boundaries are covered.

The existing two-node GB200 result is historical supporting evidence, not
validation of this head. No GB200 run is included in this update. The simplified EGM lifecycle in

title: [2/3] [Store] Add EGM-backed Store pool over NVLink
body:
## Description

Add a default-off, Provider-owned EGM Store pool for RFC #2914. HOST_NUMA
allocations are mounted as ordinary NVLink Store segments; the Master schema,
placement policy and Consumer Put/Get API are unchanged.

This is **[2/3]**: #2966 supplies the merged Transfer Engine prerequisite,
this PR adds the Store pool, and #3431 enables direct remote GPU reads. This
branch is based on `main`; #3431 remains its child.

## Implementation

- `enable_egm_store_pool` enables the pool; `egm_numa_nodes` selects `auto` or
  a comma-separated NUMA list. EGM requires `protocol=nvlink`, nonzero global
  capacity and `local_buffer_size=0`. The parsed config is passed explicitly
  through a private setup overload; auto-discovery is a named mode, not an empty
  node-list sentinel. Positional setup keeps EGM disabled.
- The normal Client initialization path can now install `nvlink` with
  discovery disabled. An EGM Provider checks the actual engine before allocating:
  it must be classic Transfer Engine with NVLink installed, not TENT or a
  different transport selected by discovery.
- The existing global-segment loop allocates and mounts EGM before local
  services start. RealClient directly owns the native HOST_NUMA allocations.
  Capacity is rounded down to the largest Store/CUDA alignment, divided across
  the selected nodes and balanced into chunks using the existing helper.
  `max_mr_size` applies only to the EGM branch, not all NVLink registrations.
- Cleanup is terminal. After callers quiesce in-flight requests, close stops
  local services and EGM offload workers, unmounts EGM segments, then
  releases backing memory. A failed unmount or CUDA release retains the affected
  allocation until process exit and logs the error; other cleanup continues.
  `close()` reports failure but clears the Python client's native references.
  Calling it again does not retry resource recovery.
- Failed or throwing mounts go through the same teardown. If there is a Client
  record, cleanup can unmount and release the allocation; a missing record or
  failed unmount retains it. The outer setup catch also covers later exceptions
  such as FileStorage construction, then rethrows. This does not promise
  synchronous removal of an uncertain remote record.

The earlier factory/hooks, caller-supplied UUID transaction, retry state machine
and global Python setup guard have been removed. Generic mount/MR failure cleanup
stays with #2336; the Python repeated-setup contract is tracked in #4294.

### Configuration

Use `MC_MS_AUTO_DISC=0` on both Provider and Consumer for explicit NVLink setup.
If discovery is enabled, `MC_FORCE_MNNVL=1` selects MNNVL on hosts with RDMA
HCAs; the EGM Provider still checks what was actually installed. Full
Provider/Consumer examples are in the updated Python API and supported-protocols
documentation.

## Scope and review size

One logical Store commit, 15 files, +790/-52 lines (before the simplification:
+2,257/-61). No Master, TransferMetadata, RDMA/TENT, wire-schema or public C++
signature changes. The GB200 harness is separate from this production branch.

title: [Store] Spread bucket offload across several disks
body:
## Description

We run SSD offload in production. It gives us a much larger cache tier than DRAM
alone and measurably lifts our KVCache hit rate. Our serving hosts, however,
have several SSDs each, and today offload can only use one of them: the rest of
the disks sit idle while the single configured disk caps both our offload
capacity and our offload bandwidth. To actually use the hardware we have, SSD
offload needs to span multiple disks.

`BucketStorageBackend` assumes a single offload root throughout: one quota, one
FIFO/LRU eviction order, one path builder. This PR lets
`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_FILE_STORAGE_PATH` take a comma-separated list of roots and
makes the bucket backend per-disk end to end. A single path keeps behaving
exactly as before — the single-disk case is just a list of length one.

RFC: #4230

**Configuration**

```bash
# Two offload disks, 200 GiB on each
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/nvme0/mooncake,/nvme1/mooncake
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_LIST=214748364800,214748364800
```

- `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_FILE_STORAGE_PATH` accepts a comma list; whitespace around
  entries is trimmed. Each root is validated on its own (`stat` of the raw list
  string would always be `ENOENT`). An empty entry (`/d0,,/d1`, a leading or
  trailing comma) is a startup error rather than being dropped: every entry
  names one disk, so dropping one would silently run on fewer disks than the
  list has entries.
- `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_LIST` is a new, optional per-disk
  quota list, positionally aligned with the path list. Unset or blank means
  the scalar `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE` applies to every disk.
  When set, it must have exactly one entry per path, and anything the backend
  would otherwise have to guess at is a startup error: an empty or unparsable
  entry, or a length that differs from the number of paths. Skipping an entry
  or reusing the last one would put a disk on its neighbour's quota, and
  falling back to the scalar would silently ignore the configured limits.
  Entries must be `> 0`, which is deliberately stricter than the scalar (where
  `<= 0` means "derive a default").
- **Limitation:** only `bucket_storage_backend` understands the list.
  `file_per_key_storage_backend` and `offset_allocator_storage_backend` use
  `storage_filepath` as a single directory, so they must stay on one path.

**Design points**

- **Per-disk accounting.** New `DiskState` holds `max_total_size`,
  `total_size`, `pending_write_size`, `pending_eviction_size`, its own
  FIFO/LRU eviction indices and its own `ActualDiskBytesUsed` scan cache.
  Quotas must not be global: a write reserved on one disk counted against
  another would make that disk evict to make room for bytes it never receives.
- **Disk selection is round-robin**, not most-free-wins. Free-space-greedy
  selection collapses onto one disk once the disks equalize, undoing the point
  of spreading writes.
- **Selection, reservation and eviction happen in one critical section**, so a
  concurrent writer cannot pick the same disk on stale free-space numbers. The
  chosen disk travels in `PendingEviction::disk_index` and every
  restore/commit/release step credits that same disk.
- **`BucketMetadata::disk_index`** routes path construction. It is not
  serialized: `Init()` re-derives it from the disk whose root the `.meta` file
  was found under, so existing on-disk data is readable without migration.
- **Watermark eviction is per-disk**, driven one disk at a time rather than off
  a single global watermark. `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_PHYSICAL_BYTES`
  likewise becomes a per-disk cap, since the `du`-equivalent scan runs per root.
- **Overlapping roots are rejected at `Init()`**, compared by path component so
  `/data/d1` is not mistaken for a child of `/data/d`.
- **The one-live-client-per-path lock from #4172 covers every root.** A client
  that shares any one disk with another live client would collide on that
  disk's bucket files, so each root gets its own `.mooncake_local_disk.lock`.
  The locks are taken after the overlap check (a root listed twice would
  otherwise fail against its own lock and hide the overlap error), and a
  client that fails part-way releases the roots it already locked.

Split into four reviewable commits:

1. `[Store] Parse multi-disk offload configuration` — config/env parsing,
   `SplitAsciiList`, `ResolveOffloadDiskPaths`, validation. Compiles and passes
   tests on its own.
2. `[Store] Spread bucket offload across several disks` — the backend
   conversion, including the per-root ownership lock.
3. `[Doc] Document multi-disk SSD offload configuration` — deployment docs for
   the new path form and quota list.
4. `[Store] Reject misaligned per-disk quota lists at startup` — review
   follow-up: empty entries in either list, and a quota list whose length does
   not match the paths, now fail startup instead of being skipped, reused or
   replaced by the scalar quota. `BucketBackendConfig::FromEnvironment()`
   returns `tl::expected`; `BucketStorageBackend::Init()` repeats the path and
   length checks for callers that skip `Validate()`.

title: [TransferEngine][Store] Fix and complete Biren (SUPA) build and device integration
body:
SUPA support was only wired into rdma_context and cuda_alike; every other vendor-conditional omitted USE_SUPA, and gpu_vendor/supa.h mapped CUDA names to non-existent `supa*` symbols, so it never compiled against a real SUPA SDK.

Transfer Engine:
- Discover GPU topology and classify device memory for SUPA (topology.cpp, memory_location.cpp).
- Enable the TCP GPU staging path for SUPA.
- Build examples and the TCP transport test with SUPA.
- Rewrite gpu_vendor/supa.h against the real SUPA API: runtime symbols use the `su` prefix, driver symbols use `sudrv`, driver enums use their `su*` names, and suMemcpyAsync takes the stream before the kind (wrapped to preserve the CUDA argument order).

Mooncake Store:
- Add AcceleratorVendor::kSupa and register the CUDA-like accelerator device.

Build:
- Include the SUPA SDK as a system include directory so its generic headers (e.g. version.h) do not shadow Mooncake headers.
- Discover the runtime library by name (libsupa/libsupa-runtime) instead of hardcoding it, and link the resolved libraries.

Docs: document -DUSE_SUPA and BIREN_HOME in build.md, quick-start.md and supported-protocols.md.

Tested on 8x Biren166M + 8x RoCE: full TE and Store build and link with -DUSE_SUPA=ON against the SUPA SDK (GPU allocation verified at runtime); the default build without USE_SUPA is unchanged.

## Description

Biren (SUPA) support existed only as a skeleton: `rdma_context.cpp` and
`cuda_alike.h` knew about `USE_SUPA`, but every other vendor-conditional omitted
it, and `gpu_vendor/supa.h` mapped the CUDA API onto `supa*` symbols that do not
exist in the real SUPA SDK (`suGetDeviceCount`, `suMallocDevice`, `sudrvMemCreate`,
...). As a result the `-DUSE_SUPA=ON` build could not compile, and even if it had,
GPU topology discovery, device-memory classification, the TCP staging path, and
the Store accelerator device would all have fallen back to CPU paths.

This change completes the Biren integration so `-DUSE_SUPA=ON` builds and works
end to end:

- **Transfer Engine**
  - `topology.cpp`: include `USE_SUPA` in the GPU topology guard so `supa:N`
    entries are discovered and NIC/GPU affinity applies.
  - `memory_location.cpp`: classify Biren device memory via `cuPointerGetAttributes`
    instead of treating it as host memory.
  - `tcp_transport.cpp` / `tcp_transport_session_impl.h`: enable GPU-aware
    staging for SUPA.
  - `example/*` and `tests/tcp_transport_test.cpp`: build the GPU paths under SUPA.
  - `gpu_vendor/supa.h`: rewrite against the actual SUPA SDK. Runtime API uses
    the `su` prefix, driver API uses `sudrv`, driver enums use their `su*` names,
    NVIDIA-only fabric/VMM concepts are dropped, and `suMemcpyAsync` (which takes
    the stream before the kind) is wrapped to keep the CUDA call order.
- **Mooncake Store**
  - Add `AcceleratorVendor::kSupa`, register the CUDA-like accelerator device, and
    enable the cuda-like registry path for SUPA.
- **Build**
  - Expose `${BIREN_HOME}/supa/include` as a **system** include dir: the SDK ships
    generic headers (notably `version.h`) that otherwise shadow Mooncake's own
    generated `version.h`.
  - Resolve the runtime library by name (`libsupa` for older SDKs,
    `libsupa-runtime` for current ones) and link the resolved library set.
- **Docs**: add Biren rows to `build.md`, `quick-start.md` and
  `supported-protocols.md`, documenting `-DUSE_SUPA=ON` and `BIREN_HOME`.

No related issue; the work aligns with the "Domestic GPU Support" milestone of
the overall roadmap.

## Description

title: fix(metadata): make rpc_meta republish idempotent in the Python server
body:
## What

The Python HTTP metadata server (`mooncake-wheel/mooncake/http_metadata_server.py`) rejected **every** duplicate `rpc_meta` key:

```python
if key.find("rpc_meta") != -1 and key in self.store:
    return web.Response(text='Duplicate rpc_meta key not allowed', status=400, ...)
```

So a node that re-publishes its own unchanged metadata (a normal occurrence on reconnect/retry) gets a `400` instead of a no-op success.

The C++ metadata server already handles this as idempotent — #2311 made it compare the stored value against the request body, returning `200 metadata unchanged` for an identical value and only rejecting a genuinely conflicting one. This PR mirrors that logic in the Python server:

```python
if key.find("rpc_meta") != -1 and key in self.store:
    if self.store[key] == data:
        return web.Response(text='metadata unchanged', status=200, ...)
    return web.Response(text='Duplicate rpc_meta key not allowed', status=400, ...)
```

## Test plan

Added `mooncake-wheel/tests/test_http_metadata_server.py`, which exercises `_handle_put` directly — no compiled engine, server, or network required (it only imports the pure-Python module and mocks the request). It covers the first write, an idempotent re-publish (the regression), a conflicting value (still rejected), and a non-`rpc_meta` overwrite.

```
python -m unittest mooncake-wheel.tests.test_http_metadata_server
# Ran 4 tests — OK
```

The idempotent-republish case fails on `main` (`400 != 200`) and passes with this change. The test is engine-free and could be wired into CI alongside `test_safetensor_functions` if desired.

title: [Store] Restore standby index tolerantly, discard ambiguous overlaps with durable repair
body:
Fixes #3760

## What

Standby promotion no longer discards the whole metadata index because one entry fails validation. `RestoreFromStandbySnapshot` runs in three phases: cheap per-entry validation (each failure skips that entry with its key and reason logged and counted on the `mooncake_ha_standby_restore_rejected_objects_total{reason}` counter), overlap resolution, then construction for the survivors only. Only segment-level structural corruption (empty name/endpoint, zero capacity) stays fail-fast, since that is a malformed context rather than one bad object.

Overlap is treated as ambiguity, not recency. The promotion input comes from `StandbyMetadataStore::Snapshot()`, which enumerates unordered maps, so no replay order reaches the promotion context and neither side of an overlap can prove it is newer. Every descriptor in a transitively overlapping group is discarded, replicas independent of the conflict are kept, and an object is dropped only when no reliable replica remains. A snapshot whose objects all fail to land returns INVALID_PARAMS instead of reporting an empty-cluster success, with one carve-out: objects rejected because the live index already holds them are not losses.

Review-driven fixes on top of that:

- Ranges join `pending_ranges` only after the object is accepted, so a rejected object never leaves a range whose owner index a later accepted object would reuse.
- Segment accounting accumulates per object and commits only once the whole object validates, so a mid-construction rejection leaves no phantom bytes behind for later capacity checks or metrics.

Out of scope here, by design: the pre-promotion dry run and promotability predicate (#3774), ReplicaID preservation (I00 dependency in the #3808 roadmap, covered by #3811), and the partial-restore serving gate. Those belong to the N07/N08 promotion contract work.

## Tests

`master_service_test.cpp` and `master_service_ha_test.cpp` pin the new semantics: per-descriptor overlap discard with independent-replica survival, transitive overlap groups, the stale-range-owner regression, accounting rollback on construction rejection, all-rejected restores returning INVALID_PARAMS, and mixed good+bad tolerance. Existing duplicate, remount, and tenant-scoping pins are unchanged.

## Verification

Local build of this repo is not possible in this environment (no rdma-core, and upstream `main` fails to compile here with the same pre-existing header errors, so this is environmental, not the change). The overlap sweep and the accounting commit flow were exercised locally through a standalone harness running the same logic against the pinned scenarios (identical, contained, transitive, and adjacent ranges, dead-replica drop, capacity rollback). clang-format 20.1.8 and codespell are clean. CI runs the full Linux build and both suites.

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3). The ambiguity-discard semantics come from the review discussion on this PR; the submitter reviewed every changed line and can defend the change end-to-end.

title: [CI] Stabilize HP TCP lane-distribution flake
body:
Fixes #4080.

`InterleavedPeersUseEveryConfiguredLane/1` (sliced read) flakes on contended CI when a recycled RPC port hits a stale process-wide pooled connection. - retry `getRemoteCached` once on `RpcServiceError` after `openRemote`
- print submit status on failure so the next flake is diagnosable

Keeps the strict per-peer lane/session assertion from #3987 (no relaxation).

Test-only.

title: [Conductor] Add KV event manager and HTTP API
body:
## Description

Fifth slice of the Mooncake Conductor upstreaming series, on top of the zmq subscriber. Wires the ingest path into the prefix index and exposes the query surface, and produces the mooncake_conductor binary:

- kvevent/event_manager.{h,cpp}: EventManager owns the indexer, the per-service ZMQ subscribers and the coroutine HTTP server. Start subscribes to every configured service concurrently and reports individual failures through the log rather than failing as a whole, so one unreachable publisher cannot block startup. Stop is idempotent. UnsubscribeFromService stops its ZMQ client outside the manager lock, because the client's loop thread can still be dispatching a batch that needs the manager. Registers five routes: /query, /register, /unregister, /services and /global_view.
- kvevent/event_handler.cpp: KVEventHandler implements the zmq EventHandler interface for the three publisher protocols, dispatching each batch to per-event handlers that translate into indexer mutations. Mooncake Store publishes one logical hash as several physical objects, such as separate key and value components, so pool_bindings_ tracks the physical set per logical key and only removes the index entry once the last component is gone.
- Handler lifecycle: MarkUnavailable stops admitting new callbacks and WaitForIdle waits for the ones already admitted, with DispatchLease releasing the in-flight count on every exit path. This is what lets a service be unsubscribed while its subscriber thread is mid-batch.
- kvevent/config.{h,cpp}: reads the static service list from CONDUCTOR_CONFIG_PATH. A missing file warns and yields an empty list; a malformed file is fatal, since silently serving no cache would be worse than failing to start.
src/main.cpp: resolves the log level, parses the config, starts the manager and HTTP server, then waits for SIGINT/SIGTERM.
Two adaptations were needed against the merged common layer, both beyond the mechanical namespace nesting:
  main.cpp consumed a LogLevel enum that no longer exists. https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3825 replaced it with LogLevelConfig, which already reports glog's own values, so the four-case switch collapses to two assignments.
  Parsing helpers come from mooncake-common rather than being reimplemented: medium normalization uses AsciiToLower (ascii_string.h) instead of a local std::tolower transform, which also drops a locale-sensitive path from a comparison against ASCII literals, and the cache-group check uses TryParseInteger<int64_t> (integer_parser.h). Both substitutions were checked against the previous local implementations over 6470 inputs, including every single byte, the medium spellings the call sites compare against, signed and unsigned int64 boundaries and overflow, embedded NULs, and padded and whitespace-wrapped forms.
  yalantinglibs is guarded with if(NOT TARGET yalantinglibs::yalantinglibs): the top-level build already provides it through mooncake-common, and its config.cmake mutates an imported target owned by the parent scope, so it cannot run twice.

Verified: builds standalone and under the top-level configuration, and conductor_test passes (169 tests across 34 suites, up from 113 across 25).

title: [Store] Add LastHitOnly lease selection to BatchProbeKey
body:
## Description

Implements the Store-side portion of [RFC #4255](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4255).
K3 prefix lookups may inspect multiple KDA checkpoints while restoring only one. This PR adds `GrantLeasePolicy` to `BatchProbeKey` to support selective lease acquisition:
- `None`: preserves the existing lease-free probe behavior.
- `LastHitOnly`: selects the last complete candidate in caller order, leases all its keys, and returns a selected-only mask.
`candidate_size` defines how many consecutive keys form a candidate. Completeness checks and lease grants run under ordered metadata-shard locks, preventing normal eviction between validation and leasing.
The policy is exposed through the C++ client/RPC layers and Python binding. Existing existence APIs, single-key probes, soft-pin behavior, and shared-group lease semantics remain unchanged. Inference-engine integration is left to follow-up PRs.

**Compatibility:** batch-probe RPC signatures change. Master, client daemon, and clients must be upgraded together; mixed-version batch-probe calls are not supported.

title: [Store] Centralize client session lifecycle and resource ownership
body:
## Description

Centralize client registration, remount readiness, heartbeat/liveness monitoring, host hints, and offboarding lifecycle in `ClientSessionManager` instead of `MasterService`.

- Add lock-scoped session admission, registration rollback, staged restore, and ordered state-change listeners.
- Keep resource cleanup in the MasterService listener while the manager owns monitoring, offboarding workers, and the snapshot cleanup barrier.
- Bind memory buffers and local-disk replicas to the exact client incarnation via read-only `ClientSessionSharedPtr`; replacing a session invalidates old segment generations rather than silently transferring their resources.
- Check local-disk staleness using the bound session rather than a point-in-time registry complement.
- Adapt snapshot restore, metrics, and tests. No RPC or snapshot wire-format change is intended.

### Related work and scope

Searched existing issues/open PRs for client sessions and liveness before opening:
- #3707 / RFC #3360 reorganize mounted-region ownership around SegmentPool and explicitly exclude ClientSession redesign. This PR retains the existing segment manager and focuses on session ownership; the two changes will need integration coordination.
- #3936 proposes mass-expiry deferral under master stalls. This PR does not add that policy.
- #4130 fixes SSD registration deduplication across different client UUIDs. This PR instead preserves exact session identity and centralizes lifecycle/admission.

This is a substantive change exceeding 500 LOC. A dedicated RFC has not yet been filed/linked. Human confirmation of reviewing every changed line is also pending; keep this PR in draft until both are addressed.

title: [CI] Add macOS build check for mooncake_master
body:
## Description

#4289 added support for building `mooncake_master` on macOS, but no CI job covers it, so Linux-only changes can silently break it again. This PR adds a separate `Build (macOS)` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci-macos.yml`) that:

- runs on the GitHub-hosted `macos-15` (arm64) runner, triggered on push/PR to `main` / `release/**` when `mooncake-*/**`, `extern/**`, `cmake/**`, `CMakeLists.txt` or the workflow itself changes, plus `workflow_dispatch`;
- checks out submodules (`extern/pybind11` is needed at configure time; Linux CI gets it from `dependencies.sh`);
- installs dependencies via Homebrew (`ninja boost fmt gflags glog jsoncpp msgpack-cxx yaml-cpp xxhash zstd openssl@3`, derived from ninja's recorded header deps and the linked libraries) and caches only the downloaded bottles (key includes the runner `ImageVersion`; `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` keeps formula versions pinned to the image);
- configures with defaults plus `-DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=OFF -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF`, builds only the `mooncake_master` target, and smoke-tests `mooncake_master --version`.

It also includes one small source fix found by the first run: `UdsAcceptor` used `std::jthread`, which is not available in the libc++ shipped with Xcode 16 (AppleClang 17, the runner's default toolchain). The acceptor never uses a `stop_token`, and `stop()` (also called by the destructor) always joins the thread; `running_` is only cleared in `stop()`. So switching to `std::thread` keeps the same behavior. `uds_transport_test` in the Linux CTest job covers it.

It is intentionally a separate workflow and not wired into `CI Gate`, so it is non-blocking for now. It can be made required once it has proven stable.

On the hosted runner the job passes in about 6 minutes: about 17s to install deps and about 5m12s to build `mooncake_master`.

title: [Store] Add the tenant-first metadata layer: tenant directory, tenant catalog, registry
body:
## Description

The tenancy layer of the tenant-first metadata model ([RFC #3670](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/3670)), split out of #3822. It adds the two types that own per-tenant metadata, under `mooncake-store/include/metadata/`, with unit tests and one benchmark. Nothing resolves through them yet, so runtime behaviour is unchanged.

The object-model types it composes (`ObjectEntry`, `ObjectIndex`, `GroupIndex`, `DynamicReplicationLeaseTable`) are already in `main` from #4161, so this diff is the tenancy layer alone.

The types:

- `metadata::TenantRegistry` — tenant id to a strong handle to that tenant's metadata, plus the lifecycle rules around it. The table is copy-on-write: a lookup is one acquire load of an immutable frame plus one map find, and a create or a remove copies the frame and publishes the replacement. One `Tenant` per id, created atomically through a factory bound at construction, and the handle is a `std::shared_ptr` rather than a template parameter, so the guarantee that a loaded frame stays alive is structural.
- `metadata::Tenant` — one tenant's metadata: the object route (`ObjectIndex`), the group table (`GroupIndex`, membership plus one shared replica-action lease per group), the in-flight replica-action lease table, the promotion-candidate index and the bound quota account. Those interfaces are private, and callers go through the tenant's own operations.

What the layer guarantees, and where each guarantee lives:

- **Reads take no lock.** `TenantRegistry::Lookup` loads the published frame, and the handle it returns keeps that frame alive, so a publish in flight cannot invalidate a lookup.
- **A tenant is built once.** `GetOrCreateTenant` re-checks under the write lock before running the factory, so concurrent callers for an absent tenant all receive the winner's handle, and only one tenant is built — fully initialized before it is published.
- **A walk sees one frame.** `Visit` passes const handles taken from the frame it loaded, so a callback cannot replace a published entry; a publish made from inside the callback is visible to the next walk only.
- **A handle keeps an entry alive, not current.** `TenantRegistry::Remove` drops a tenant from the registry while handles callers already hold stay valid, and a later create for the same id builds a fresh tenant. An object is recognised by the handle the route publishes: an entry instance stands for exactly one publication, which `ObjectIndex::Insert` asserts, so `EraseObjectIf` compares handles and no caller records a number to tell its object apart from a replacement.
- **Publication and teardown are atomic per object.** `Tenant::InsertObject` wires the route slot and the group lease under the entry's own lock, so a grouped object is never reachable before its group lease is in place, and a rejected insert registers nothing. `RemoveObject` is the single teardown entry point: it drops everything a key carries — route slot, group membership, the replica-action leases of that key and its promotion-candidate index entry — so those records cannot be left disagreeing about a key. `ResetDynamicReplicationState` is the other path that ends a lease: it clears the pending proposal, the cooldown and the leases while leaving the object routed.
- **A teardown cannot outrun a republish.** `RemoveObject` settles ownership and drops a key's records under one hold of the route lock. A slot still holding the entry means the records are its, so they go with the slot; a slot holding another entry means a newer publication of the same key owns them, so none of them is touched; an empty slot means no publication owns them, so they go as well, which is what undoes the records a publish registered before it failed. A teardown therefore never drops what a newer publication of the same key just registered.
- **Lock order runs one way: entry lock, then the route lock, then the tenant's own indexes.** Nothing is held across a public call except in `RemoveObject`, which holds the route lock while it drops a key's records for the reason above; nothing takes the route lock while holding one of those indexes. `RemoveObject` requires the caller to hold the entry's own lock, which is what keeps a publication still wiring its state from being torn down half-registered.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**
```bash
cmake --build build -j64
ctest -R "metadata_tenant|object_entry|object_index|group_index|dynamic_replication_lease_table|master_service|master_scenario" -j8
```

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done (benchmark below)

- Build: the targets this change touches compile and link with no errors and no warnings.
- 44 cases pass across the six metadata suites: `object_entry_test` (3), `object_index_test` (6), `dynamic_replication_lease_table_test` (7), `group_index_test` (6), `metadata_tenant_test` (16) and `metadata_tenant_registry_test` (6). The master service and scenario suites in the selection still run on the shard model and are unchanged here.
- The new tests exercise the guarantees above: removing a tenant keeps an outstanding handle alive while the same id resolves to a fresh tenant, concurrent get-or-create builds one tenant and hands every racer the winner, lookups interleaved with 50k remove-and-create rounds never see a tenant before it is built, a walk iterates the frame it loaded and reaches every tenant, a grouped insert shares one lease and joins the group, `EraseObjectIf` compares handles, and `RemoveObject` is covered on all three outcomes it settles: it drops every record of the entry the slot holds, leaves a replacement and its records untouched, and still clears a key whose slot is already gone.
- Formatting: `./scripts/code_format.sh -b origin/main --changed-lines --check` with clang-format 20.1.8 reports no violation.
- `group_index_contention_bench` (new) measures the group table's write path. The stripe count is the one knob on that table and it trades per-tenant memory for write concurrency, so one run instantiates a table per stripe count and reports member writes per second, a write being one registration plus the member leaving the window, 2 s per point:

| stripes | table bytes per tenant | 1 thread | 4 threads | 16 threads | 32 threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 128 | 384k | 150k | 192k | 174k |
| 16 | 1,928 | 371k | 887k | 951k | 1.27M |
| 32 | 3,848 | 380k | 1.05M | 2.27M | 1.67M |
| 64 | 7,688 | 375k | 1.09M | 3.03M | 3.61M |
| 128 | 15,368 | 376k | 1.22M | 3.85M | 4.87M |
| 256 | 30,728 | 369k | 1.26M | 4.46M | 5.64M |

  One stripe loses throughput as threads are added, 64 stripes recovers most of that loss at 7.7 kB per tenant, and 256 stripes reaches 5.6M at 32 threads for four times the memory. `GroupIndex` is therefore `StripedGroupIndex<64>`, which the alias comment in `include/group_index.h` records. title: [Bugfix][Store] Read file-backed replicas in session API
body:
## Description

Fixes #3658.

After #3903, get sessions already support MEMORY (zero-copy) and DFS (staging + scatter). SSD-only / file-backed keys still failed session start with `702 INVALID_REPLICA` because `SelectSessionReplica` and the classify/execute pipeline only handled MEMORY and DFS.

This PR extends that same prepare → classify → execute pipeline (no separate packing layer):

1. **`SelectSessionReplica`**: after MEMORY / DFS, also accept a complete `LOCAL_DISK` or `DISK` replica. NOF-only keys still return `INVALID_REPLICA`.
2. **`classify_session_range_read_requests`**: route `LOCAL_DISK` → `local_disk_requests`, `DISK` → `disk_requests`.
3. **LOCAL_DISK** (`execute_session_local_disk_range_reads`): group by owner endpoint; restore each unique key once via shared `restore_offload_objects(..., allow_pinned=false)` (RPC into the owner's TE-registered client buffer — never the unregistered pinned arena); then `Client::BatchTransferReadOffloadRanges` from restored pointer + `src_offset` into already `register_buffer`'d destinations. The reader does **not** need a setup local buffer (`local_buffer_size=0` works). Same-node GPU destinations also go through TE (no offload `kLocalAddress` memcpy on the session path).
4. **DISK** (`execute_session_disk_range_reads`): one `Client::BatchGet` into a temp host buffer, then scatter by `src_offset`. Keys fail if the client has no allocator.
5. **Shared restore helper**: sequential `batch_get_into_offload_object_internal` now uses the same `restore_offload_objects` / `OffloadRestoreLease` (default `allow_pinned=true` so memcpy into the pinned arena remains available).

Duplicate keys restore once and scatter many times. Invalid ranges do not block valid entries. Lease is checked locally after transfer. Offload GC TTL rewrites only successful scatters to `OBJECT_HAS_LEASE`. No session-level object pin.

## Relation to #3903

#3903 landed the DFS session path and the shared pipeline. This branch was rebased onto main: redundant DFS / `MultiBufferRangeRequest` work from earlier revisions was dropped; only LOCAL_DISK / DISK session reads and the shared offload restore helper remain.

title: [CI] Write the sccache GHA cache only from push and scheduled builds
body:
## Description

Make PR builds read the sccache GitHub Actions cache without writing to it. Only `push` and `schedule` runs write.

**Why.** GitHub lets a PR run read caches from its own ref and from its base branch (`main`), but not from other PRs. So a PR run's sccache writes only help that same PR's later runs. They still count toward the repo's 10 GB Actions cache limit, though.

Snapshot on 2026-09-24 08:05 UTC:

- The cache held 7351 entries (11.0 GB), all of them `sccache/*`. That is over the limit, so least-recently-used eviction is running.
- 2700 entries (5.46 GB) belonged to just 7 open PRs.
- The least-recently-used entry left in the cache was last read at 06:49. In other words, any entry that goes about 75 minutes without a read gets evicted, and that includes `main`'s.

The effect shows up in CI logs:

- **Main's cache works.** A fork PR's first run (`vin/gid-fix`, run 35947527377) hit 243 of 252 compiles in `build-wheel (3.10)`. Those hits could only have come from `main`'s entries.
- **A PR's own entries rarely survive long enough to matter.** For `tent-diagnostic-core`, two pushes 48 minutes apart took tent-ci hits from about 60% to about 98%. Two pushes about 4 hours apart stayed near 60%, because the earlier entries had been evicted.
- **PR writes push out main configurations that run less often.** In PR 4305's runs, the new arm64 EFA jobs hit 0 of 230 compiles on two pushes 66 minutes apart.

With PRs read-only, the whole cache goes to `main` and `release/**` entries, which every PR can read.

The E2E workflow (`e2e-ci.yml`) is also affected. Its `pull_request_target` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers build PR code through `ci_rocm.yml` under `main`'s cache scope. Those builds now read the cache but no longer write into `main`'s.

**How.** Set `SCCACHE_GHA_RW_MODE` (supported since sccache 0.18, the version the action installs) wherever `SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED` is set for a workflow that PR code can reach:

- `ci.yml`
- `ci_rocm.yml`
- `_build-wheel.yaml`
- `_build-efa-wheel.yaml`

In reusable workflows, `github.event_name` is the caller's event, so the rule follows the trigger that started the run. `nightly.yml` only runs on schedule or manual dispatch and is unchanged.

**Trade-off.** A PR no longer reuses its own objects from its previous push. Under the current ~75-minute eviction window, that reuse was already unreliable.

title: [Store] Persist and recover DFS shard allocator metadata
body:
## Description

Implements standalone DFS shard allocator recovery proposed in #3819, rebased onto the current `ShardAllocator` interface after the allocator rename and bucket backend addition.

The shard allocator now persists allocation ownership in per-shard checkpoints and WALs, then reconciles recovered allocations with standalone Master snapshots before serving requests. In particular:

- Persist `ALLOC` before exposing a descriptor and `RELEASE` before reusing a deferred extent.
- Recover from checksummed checkpoints and WAL records, with configurable compaction.
- Seal shard allocations during snapshot reconciliation, retain matching replicas, prune stale descriptors, and quarantine orphan allocations.
- Reject incomplete, corrupt, or incompatible sidecars, and preserve allocation ownership across online shard expansion and restart.
- Carry a persistent allocation ID in DFS descriptors to reject stale references after extent reuse.

The new immutable bucket allocator remains a separate DFS mode. This PR applies metadata persistence and snapshot reconciliation to `ShardAllocator` only; bucket mode retains its own allocation and eviction behavior and remains incompatible with snapshot restore. Compatibility validation uses stable per-shard identity instead of total shard count. The WAL compaction setting is `MOONCAKE_DFS_METADATA_WAL_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_BYTES`.

### Compatibility and scope

The client data path and existing Put/Upsert RPC signatures remain unchanged. Existing roots containing only `.data` files cannot be migrated in place; upgrade and rollback require a new empty shard DFS root. HA, OpLog recovery, standby promotion, and multi-tenant DFS remain unsupported. Metadata persistence does not add data-file `fsync` durability.

title: [Store] HA optlog support redis backed
body:
## Description
A Redis HA cluster could already elect a leader, but the batch OpLog could not follow it. OrderedOpLogWriter and the standby reader talk to a HaKvBackend: one compare-and-swap transaction per batch, then a lexicographic range to catch up. Only the etcd backend implemented that contract, so --enable_oplog=true with ha_backend_type=redis was rejected at startup, and a cluster that already ran Redis still needed a second etcd just to store acknowledged batches. Leadership and the log are separate; this change gives the log a Redis implementation and leaves snapshots on etcd.

What changes

RedisHaKvBackend implements the existing KV contract. The writer, the standby reader, and the applier are unchanged. CreateHaKvBackend is the only place that opens the backend, and the master writer, ClaimProducerView, and the standby follower all go through it. etcd still takes the etcd branch. k8s is rejected. A build without STORE_USE_REDIS or STORE_USE_ETCD returns UNAVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_MODE from the factory, so the no-backend stub that aborts the process is never called.

Logical keys stay /oplog/{cluster}/producer_view, durable_prefix, and batches/{id}. Redis stores the bytes at mooncake-store/{cluster}/oplog/... and orders those logical keys in the ZSET mooncake-store/{tag}/oplog-index. The hash tag puts the index and the records on one slot, so the Lua script is valid on Redis Cluster. The connection is the backend's own; it is not the connection the leader renew thread uses.

One acknowledged batch is one EVAL. The script checks that producer_view equals the claimed view and durable_prefix equals the expected prefix, then writes the batch record and advances the prefix. A failed compare returns ETCD_TRANSACTION_FAIL. A reply that never comes back resets the connection and returns ETCD_OPERATION_ERROR; the existing read-back path treats that as ambiguous and reconciles. kCreateRevisionEquals returns INVALID_PARAMS before any command is sent. Redis has no create revision, and the snapshot maintenance lease still needs one.

Splitting the log from the snapshot leaves two races the commit of a batch already had, and the Redis mapping has to preserve them:

A range or a delete is [begin, end). limit 0 means the whole interval; a Redis COUNT of 0 would return nothing. The next page starts at last_key + '\0'. Bounds that are empty, a single NUL, or begin > end are rejected, and one transaction may not touch two cluster ids.

A dropped connection can hide a script that did commit. The backend does not retry that call. The caller reads the prefix back and continues from what Redis actually stored.

Behavior change: --enable_oplog on Redis. With STORE_USE_REDIS and a connstring, ha_backend_type=redis now creates the batch writer and the standby follows the same Redis. Before, that combination fataled, and an empty connstring still skips the writer. enable_oplog_snapshot and snapshot restore still require ha_backend_type=etcd. Redis has to run AOF with appendfsync everysec or always; a restart without it can drop batches the master has already acknowledged.

Smaller changes:

HaBackendSupportsOpLog is one switch on HABackendType. Adding a backend is that case plus a factory branch.
The shard scan copies buffer descriptors only for replicas on the segments being re-adopted. The Redis range copies values only for keys inside the requested interval.
NoF placeholder allocators stay out of this path. Nothing in the Redis backend adopts them.
The deployment guide states that the same Redis holds leader election and the batch log, and that clients still use the redis:// master address. The restore-side log is unchanged.
CreateRevisionCompareIsRejected always runs. The four integration tests run only when the binary is built with STORE_USE_REDIS and --redis_endpoint is set; gtest_main does not parse gflags, so this target supplies its own main.

title: [Store] Integrate managed weight revisions with Master and HA
body:
## Description

This PR integrates the managed weight metadata model introduced by #4116 into
Mooncake Store's Master and HA paths. It is the second implementation step for 
revision-level model-weight management in Mooncake Store.

The PR:

- publishes manifest-backed weight revisions through `MasterService` and the
  Store RPC layer;
- fences revision access with leases so readers and destructive lifecycle

- replicates weight metadata mutations through the existing operation log;
- includes weight metadata in Master snapshots and restores it on standby and

title: ci: build aarch64 EFA wheels
body:
## Summary
Build and publish aarch64 variants of the AWS EFA wheels (`mooncake-transfer-engine-efa`, `-efa-cuda13`, `-efa-non-cuda`) alongside the existing x86_64 wheels. The default wheels already ship aarch64; the EFA ones were x86_64 only. aws-efa-installer supports aarch64, so this unblocks EFA on Graviton and GB200 (p6e-gb200).

## Changes
- `_build-efa-wheel.yaml`: new `architecture` input (`x86_64` | `arm64`, default `x86_64`).
  - arm64 runs on `ubuntu-22.04-arm`, same as `_build-wheel.yaml`.
  - The libfabric library path is resolved with `uname -m` instead of hardcoding `x86_64-linux-gnu`.
  - New step checks that the wheel platform tag matches the target architecture.
  - arm64 artifact names get a `-arm64` suffix. x86_64 names are unchanged, so the existing publish patterns (`mooncake-wheel-efa-py*`, `-cuda13-py*`, `-non-cuda-py*`) collect both architectures without matching other variants.
- `release-efa*.yaml`: each workflow now builds an `[x86_64, arm64]` matrix with `fail-fast: false`. The PyPI package names are unchanged, and pip picks the wheel by platform tag.
- `ci_efa.yml`: adds one cuda13 / py3.12 / arm64 build to PR CI.

## Testing
- [x] actionlint passes on the changed workflows.
- [ ] PR CI arm64 EFA build passes.
- [ ] aarch64 wheel tested over EFA on 2x Graviton EFA instances (hpc7g / c7gn), DRAM path.

title: [Store] Add P01 codec evidence and real-etcd replay checks
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4160/files) against `main`.

## Description

Implements the **P01 codec evidence experiment** in #3808 without changing production persistence or writer selection.

**Depends on #4141 (W02), pinned to `e92af584fa106668c3e311b66e1592bd8922b42b`.** This is a separate dependent branch, not an addition to the W02 PR. Until W02 merges, this draft's main-based diff includes its two prerequisite commits; the P01-specific commit adds only `benchmarks/oplog_codec/`. Rebase/drop those prerequisites after #4141 merges.

- Compare production JsonCpp JSON, a same-library nlohmann JSON/base64 control, CBOR, and MessagePack using production batch validators/checksums.
- Add six opaque-payload profiles and five generated production-schema profiles with actual struct_pack metadata/Segment serialization.
- Exercise the latest asynchronous durable awaiter through production writer/storage and a test-only backend bridge on isolated real etcd namespaces.
- Restart etcd, audit every acknowledged operation, replay through production OpLogApplier/StandbyMetadataStore, and check fencing/corruption and duplicate replay.
- Publish two complete raw measurement passes, summaries, environment/hash metadata, and the eight-case E2E report under `benchmarks/oplog_codec/results/2026-09-16/`.

Generated-schema payload sizes shrink approximately 24–26%. Final-pass observed CPU ratios versus the same-library control span 3.00–14.36× encode and 1.37–3.57× decode. These are shared-host codec microbenchmarks with substantial variability, **not service-throughput gains or a CBOR/MessagePack selection**. The test bridge's transcoding overhead is not timed. RPC/HA promotion/resource rebuilding is outside scope; P02/P03 remain conditional.

This is benchmark/test-only work covered by the P01 roadmap, not a >500 LOC production architectural change. Kept draft for the W02 dependency and human review.
