title: [Store] Track requested and reserved allocation sizes without changing wire formats
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4222/files) against `main`.

## Description

Related to #3808 (E01). This is the **runtime accounting-fields slice**: an
`AllocatedBuffer` now distinguishes the caller's requested byte count from the
extent its allocator actually reserved, for both the CacheLib and
OffsetAllocator backends.

E01 in the roadmap reads "Distinguish requested bytes from allocator-reserved
bytes while keeping old descriptors readable". This patch does that at runtime
and keeps old descriptors readable by rebuilding the extent from real backend
metadata after a restore. It deliberately **adds no field to any writer**, so it
does not claim completion of a persisted descriptor schema extension. If a
persisted field is what E01 is meant to require, that is a separate wire
contract and this patch is its prerequisite, not its substitute.

What changes:

- `AllocatedBuffer::requested_size()` names the existing `size()` value;
  `size()` keeps its meaning as the transfer length for the descriptor and the
  requested-based usage counters.
- `AllocatedBuffer::reserved_size()` returns `std::optional<std::size_t>`.
  `nullopt` means "no physical allocation has been reconstructed yet" — never
  zero, never `requested_size()`.
- The owning constructor now takes `reserved_size` as a **required** parameter,
  so every production allocation site had to state where its value comes from.
  All five sites were audited: CacheLib fresh allocate, CacheLib import, Offset
  fresh allocate, Offset import, and the descriptor rebinding in
  `Serializer<AllocatedBuffer>::deserialize`.
- CacheLib reads the allocation class size from the chunk's own slab header
  (`MemoryAllocator::getAllocInfo(...).allocSize`), for fresh allocations and for
  `importAllocations` alike. `padding_size = max(requested, kMinSliceSize)` is
  only the allocation *input*; class rounding can reserve more, so it is no
  longer treated as the extent.
- OffsetAllocator reads the real node extent (`node.dataSize <<
  multiplier_bits`) while the allocation lock is already held and carries it on
  the handle. `createHandleAtNode` and the new bounds-checked
  `allocationReservedSize()` read the same source, so a handle rebuilt from
  persisted state reports the extent it was actually allocated with instead of
  re-deriving it from the current rounding rules. `OFFSET_ALLOCATOR_NOT_ROUND_UP`
  and legacy size classes therefore stay correct.
- Both backends **enforce** `reserved_size() >= requested_size()`. An extent that
  is missing or smaller than the request rolls the allocation back (the raw chunk
  is freed / the node released), records no usage, and fails the call. `nullopt`
  is consequently reachable only for buffers that own no physical allocation —
  it is not a silent fallback for a failed lookup.
- `ImportCachelibBufferAllocator` resolves every extent **before** the first
  `adoptImportedBuffer` call records usage, so a partially adopted import cannot
  publish accounting.
- `AllocatedBuffer` move construction/assignment were declared in the header but
  never defined, so no object-level move existed. They are now defined so the new
  field follows ownership: the destination releases its previous allocation
  exactly once, self-assignment is an explicit no-op, and the moved-from object
  owns nothing. `SegmentLifetime::isAvailable()` also treats a moved-out token as
  unavailable instead of dereferencing a null pointer.

**This changes two public constructor signatures** (`AllocatedBuffer` and
`OffsetAllocationHandle` gained a required parameter), which is a source-level
breaking change for any out-of-tree caller. In-tree call sites are updated,
including the test double in `tests/test_buffer_allocator.h`.

Requested-based accounting is untouched: `RecordAllocation`,
`RecordDeallocation`, `SetUsageBytesForRestore` and `GetUsageBytes` still operate
on requested bytes, and `deallocate` still frees the whole chunk/node and
decrements by `size()`.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Breaking change

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**
```bash
# Focused suites, both revisions (base 2abe68b0 and the patched tree)
ctest --test-dir <build> --output-on-failure --no-tests=error -R \
  '^(buffer_allocator_test|offset_allocator_test|serializer_test|replica_allocator_test|segment_pool_test|master_metrics_test|master_snapshot_codec_test|store_resource_snapshot_codec_test)$'

# New E01 cases only
build/mooncake-store/tests/buffer_allocator_test --gtest_filter='*E01*'
build/mooncake-store/tests/offset_allocator_test  --gtest_filter='*E01*'

# Store-path integration suites, both revisions
build/mooncake-store/tests/master_service/dsl/master_scenario_test
build/mooncake-store/tests/dummy_client_get_buffer_test

# Sanitizers (repo-supported option + UBSan), separate build directory
cmake -S . -B build-asan -DENABLE_ASAN=ON -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all" \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined"
ctest --test-dir build-asan -R '^(buffer_allocator_test|offset_allocator_test)$'
```

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done (describe below)

Environment: Ubuntu 22.04.5, g++ 11.4.0, CMake 3.27.0, `Unix Makefiles`,
`RelWithDebInfo`. Host-side work; no GPU used. Base SHA
`2abe68b0f89238cda206bdb41d71ab6fc52f6469` (upstream/main at the time of the
work — upstream has since advanced).

| Check | Base | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Focused suites (8 targets) | 8/8 pass | 8/8 pass |
| `master_scenario_test` | 44/44 pass | 44/44 pass |
| `dummy_client_get_buffer_test` | 12 pass, 2 skipped | 12 pass, 2 skipped |
| ASan + Leak + UBSan (`buffer_allocator_test`, `offset_allocator_test`) | — | 34 and 61 tests pass, no sanitizer report |

18 new cases are added (13 in `buffer_allocator_test`, 5 in
`offset_allocator_test`) covering per-backend reserved extents against
**independent** oracles (the configured CacheLib allocation-class set; the
OffsetAllocator free-space delta — never the same helper that produced the
value), move and self-move, import with holes, restored-handle extent, CXL offset
handling, concurrency, failure paths and zero-length behaviour. Zero-length
behaviour was additionally measured with a probe binary built against both
revisions: identical output.

**Cross-version wire compatibility.** A fixture tool was compiled against both
revisions with identical flags and link line, so the two binaries differ only by
this patch. It emits the exact `Serializer<AllocatedBuffer>` bytes and reads them
back:

- `base emit` and `patched emit` are **byte-identical** (same sha256).
- old→old, **old→new**, new→new and **new→old** all pass with 0 failures over
  `requested = {477, 4097, 100000}` on an OFFSET and a CACHELIB region.
- The patched reader reconstructs, with no persisted field at all:
  OFFSET `477 → 480`, `4097 → 4608`, `100000 → 106496`;
  CACHELIB `477 → 480`, `4097 → 4544`, `100000 → 103496`. The two backends
  legitimately disagree for the same request, which is precisely why each must
  report its own metadata.
- Wire shape is asserted directly: every buffer record is a 5-element array and
  every offset record's nested handle is a 3-element array.

**Performance.** The expected cost is one extra metadata read per allocation (a
slab-header read for CacheLib, one node read under the already-held lock for
Offset), against 250.8–299.9 ns/op measured at one thread. A paired 72-arm
fresh-process screen could not resolve it and is reported as inconclusive: the
A/A control, which runs the *same baseline binary in both arms*, reported a
nominally significant **+11.72 %** (95 % interval [+0.72, +23.93]), and every
A/P interval crossed zero. No performance claim is made in either direction; a
verdict needs a quiet, dedicated machine with clock/power stabilisation.

**Object size:** `AllocatedBuffer` 176 → 208 B and `OffsetAllocationHandle`
40 → 56 B (`std::optional` fields). This is per live replica, not per segment.

**Not tested:** real CXL / NoF device I/O (no hardware; the address-representation
half is covered by a metadata-level test that confirms a CXL offset is *not*
attributed to slab metadata), and real-etcd HA restore E2E.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] I have formatted my code using `./scripts/code_format.sh`
- [ ] I have run pre-commit on the files changed in this PR and all hooks pass
- [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable)
- [x] I have added tests to prove my changes are effective
- [ ] For changes >500 LOC: I have filed an RFC issue

Notes on the unticked boxes, so nothing is implied that was not done:

- **`code_format.sh`**: the script hard-requires clang-format 20, which is not
  available on the host used for this work. Instead `git clang-format-14 --diff`
  was applied to the changed lines only; 20 format hunks were fixed and 0 remain.
  Whole-file formatting was deliberately avoided because clang-format 14 also
  disagrees with the committed style in untouched regions. A maintainer run of
  `scripts/code_format.sh` is the authority.
- **pre-commit**: not installed on the host. `git diff --check` is clean and the
  changed files end with a newline, which is what the local hooks would assert.
- **documentation**: no user-facing documentation describes allocation
  accounting, so there is nothing to update; the semantics are documented in the
  new API comments.
- **RFC**: no separate RFC was filed. The work is tracked by the E01 item in
  #3808, and this PR proposes the runtime-first scope boundary explicitly rather
  than assuming it.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (specify below)

AI tools assisted with drafting the implementation, the tests, and the
measurement/evidence harness (paired A/B screening, the cross-revision wire
fixture tool, and the sanitizer runs). All results in this description were
produced by commands run on the target host, and the human submitter has
reviewed the change and is responsible for understanding and defending it.

Test and benchmark sources are retained locally; the validation results below refer to those local files.

title: [Build] Support building mooncake_master on macOS
body:
## Description

**Depends on #4016.** This branch is stacked on #4016; only the last commit
(`[Build] Support building mooncake_master on macOS`)
belongs to this PR. The #4016 commits will drop out of the diff once it merges.

#4016 fixes the `linux/memfd.h` error from #3926, but the Store build still
fails on macOS after it. This PR makes `mooncake_master` build, link, and run
on macOS arm64 (Apple Clang 21) with `-DWITH_STORE=ON -DWITH_TE=OFF`.

### Decouple the master from the TE metadata plugin

The master linked `transfer_metadata_plugin` for a single reason: it used
`MetadataStoragePlugin` to DELETE a timed-out client's `ram/` and `rpc_meta/`
keys on a separately deployed HTTP metadata server. Without TE, that target
does not exist and the link fails.

- Add `httpDelete()` next to the existing `httpGet()` in `common/network`
  (ylt `coro_http_client`), and use it for the remote cleanup. The key
  encoding (`?key=<url-encoded>`), the 3 s timeout, and the "200 only" success
  rule match the old plugin.
- `mooncake_store_master` no longer links `transfer_metadata_plugin`, and the
  cleanup path no longer depends on the TE `USE_HTTP` option.
- Remote cleanup now accepts only `http://` endpoints, because the ylt HTTP
  client is built without TLS. A `https://` endpoint logs a warning and
  disables remote cleanup, the same way etcd/redis endpoints are handled.

### Portability fixes hit by the master build

- ibverbs: disable yalantinglibs ibverbs RPC on macOS (`FindYLT.cmake`). Guard
  `init_ibv()` and `ib_socket_t` uses with `YLT_ENABLE_IBV`. If
  `MC_RPC_PROTOCOL=rdma` is set in a build without it, log a warning and fall
  back to TCP. `ClientRequester` now reuses `detail::MaybeEnableRdmaSocketConfig`.
- NUMA: link `numa` only on Linux; `bindToSocket()` in TE `common.h` returns
  `ERR_NUMA` on non-Linux platforms, like the existing "NUMA unavailable" path.
- Bundled fmt 8.0.1: newer Clang rejects `FMT_STRING` with format specs in
  the bigint formatter as a non-constant expression; use plain literals there.
- Missing `#include <shared_mutex>` in `master_snapshot_manager.h`. libc++
  does not pull it in transitively, and Clang silently typo-corrected it to
  `std::timed_mutex`.
- `lease.h`: explicit `duration_cast`, since `system_clock` is microseconds on
  libc++.
- `size_t` vs `uint64_t` mismatches (`std::max` in `allocator.cpp`,
  `GetUInt64` for `cxl_size`).
- `uds_transport.cpp`: set `FD_CLOEXEC` via `fcntl` when `SOCK_CLOEXEC` is
  unavailable; cast `timeval` fields explicitly.
- `local_ssd`: add the Boost include directory via `find_path` (Homebrew
  headers are not on the default search path).

### Out of scope

- The Store client side (`mooncake_store_client_objects`) and the unit tests
  that link it still do not build on macOS (TE headers, mmap/NVMe ioctl, ...).
- `uds_transport` compiles but uses Linux abstract-namespace sockets, so it
  does not work at runtime on macOS. Only the client uses it.

## Module

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

- [ ] Reshard (`mooncake-reshard`)

## How Has This Been Tested?

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DWITH_STORE=ON -DWITH_TE=OFF \
      -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

# default WITH_TE=ON still configures

title: [Store] Add a dual-format OpLog batch reader (JSON + framed binary)
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4194/files) against `main`.

## Summary

P02 reader half of the batch-OpLog format migration. The production writer is
unchanged: it still emits the existing JSON batch record, and this PR adds no
writer selector, no environment variable, no default switch and no history
migration.

What it does:

- adds **one** format/version dispatch point at the existing
  `DecodeOpLogBatchRecord` entry, whose signature is unchanged. A complete
  binary magic selects the binary decoder, a non-empty truncation of the magic
  is its own error, and every other input goes to the **unchanged JSON reader
  exactly once** (no `try A then B` fallback chain), so the historical
  whitespace/BOM/parser acceptance domain, base64 canonicality checks and error
  strings do not change;
- adds a single binary encoding (MessagePack body inside a fixed 16-byte
  envelope) decoded by a bounded reader written for this six-element schema
  only: declared lengths are checked against the remaining bytes and the field
  budgets before any allocation, only unsigned integer encodings are accepted,
  `payload` must be `BIN` (STR/EXT rejected, including extension subtypes),
  `op_type` is range-checked before narrowing, and the whole body must be
  consumed;
- verifies the **existing canonical logical batch checksum**, so both physical
  encodings of the same logical batch agree on the checksum value. This
  deliberately does not change the JSON checksum algorithm, the JSON writer
  output, the durable prefix encoding or the snapshot encodings. A consequence
  worth stating: this version therefore does **not** remove the base64/JSON
  projection cost, so the P01 decode-speed multiples do not carry over to it;
- keeps failure atomic: validation happens on local candidates and the caller's
  record is assigned exactly once on success, so a failed decode cannot expose
  half a batch.

Startup prefix validation, the writer's ambiguous-transaction readback and the
batch auditor inherit the capability through the shared entry point with no
further edits.

## Testing

Executed on Ubuntu 22.04 / gcc 11.4.0 (RelWithDebInfo, `USE_CUDA=OFF`,
`WITH_EP=OFF`).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `oplog_batch_dual_codec_test` (new, 34 cases) | pass |
| `oplog_batch_codec_test` | 32 pass |
| `oplog_batch_storage_test` (+8 new mixed-format cases) | 64 pass |
| `oplog_batch_standby_reader_test` | 26 pass |
| `oplog_applier_test` | 28 pass |
| `ordered_oplog_writer_test` | 50 pass |
| `oplog_batch_auditor_test` | 8 pass |

CTest registration was verified before running, so an empty pattern cannot look
like a pass: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 7`.

The new suite covers every valid `OpType`; byte-exact payload/key preservation
including all 256 byte values, embedded NUL and non-UTF-8 keys; every truncation
point of a valid record; header field corruption, trailing bytes and a
concatenated second body; strict type rejection (signed ints, float, bool, nil,
maps, payload as STR, payload as EXT, out-of-range `op_type` without narrowing);
sequence/range/checksum rejection including single-bit flips; forged
`bin32`/`array32` lengths failing without large allocation; and fixed-seed
property tests (1000 constrained batches round-trip and agree with the JSON
reader). The JSON writer output for four fixtures is asserted byte-for-byte
against bytes captured from a pristine pre-change build.

Separately built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`:
7/7 suites pass, 0 sanitizer findings. `libFuzzer` was not run.

A real-etcd 3.3.25 integration harness (producer in one process, etcd restart,
reader in a fresh process) confirms the all-JSON control replays end to end and
that the unchanged writer appends JSON after the terminal batch; five
corrupt-history scenarios fail closed.

## Known blocker (not fixed here)

The production etcd **Range** read path is not binary-transparent: the Go bridge
marshals range results through `encoding/json`, which rewrites every byte
`>= 0x80` to U+FFFD. A controlled probe shows a 256-byte value returning as 512
bytes from `Range` while `Get` is byte-exact. So `ReadBatch` (single key) reads a
framed binary batch correctly end to end, while `ReadBatchesAfter` cannot deliver
binary bytes, which means range-based replay of binary history cannot succeed
yet.

This is pre-existing infrastructure behaviour and outside the reader diff, but
it must be resolved before any binary writer can ship. Options: hex/base64 the
range response, return lengths plus raw pointers, or read the replay range by
key. Happy to take whichever direction maintainers prefer.

## Open gates

- Maintainer approval of the physical codec, the envelope, and the
  checksum-reuse decision. The magic, `codec_id`, envelope version and the
  checksum choice are **local proposals**, not project-assigned values.
- The etcd Range bridge fix above.

Related: #3808 (HA/OpLog roadmap), #4141 (W02, merged), #4160 (P01 evidence,
open). Built on top of the W02 work already in `main`; it does not duplicate it
and does not implement P03.

title: [TE] Bound pooled TCP admission by queued bytes
body:
## Description

Classic TCP currently bounds each connection group's waiting work by item
count. Because each item retains its source payload until it starts or leaves
the waiting queues, large requests can retain a much larger byte extent than
the item limits suggest. This became more important after #3710 raised the
default queue and pending-admission limits to 65,535. Its review identified a
byte-based limit as follow-up work.

This change adds the opt-in `MC_TCP_MAX_QUEUED_BYTES_PER_PEER` setting. For each
TCP `ConnectionKey`, it bounds:

```text
sum(queue.length) + sum(pending_admissions.length)
```

A request that would exceed the limit receives the existing `QUEUE_FULL`
terminal result. Moving an item from pending admission to the queue is
accounting-neutral; its charge is released when it starts on a lane or leaves a
waiting container through timeout, error, retirement, or shutdown.

Unset or `0` preserves existing behavior. Active lanes are excluded because
their count is already bounded by `MC_TCP_LANES_PER_PEER`. The limit remains
opt-in because selecting a nonzero default requires representative
slow/stalled-peer and caller-recovery measurements.

Admission is per transport work item, not atomic over a multi-descriptor
`batchTransferSync` call. An earlier descriptor can be accepted before a later
one is rejected. The documentation therefore warns callers not to treat a
nonzero batch result as proof that no destination bytes changed or that all
source buffers can immediately be released.

This is a resource-admission bound, not a throughput or RSS-reduction claim.

Related: #2930, #3710, #3446

title: [TENT] Half-Open rail state machine + admit/isAvailable split
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #3946 (defect A + log rate-limiting). #3946 capped burst-escalation (cooldown 30s vs 300s) and rate-limited the failure-storm logs, but left `available()` as a mutating admit used as a predicate and dropped Half-Open/probing to this follow-up. A reviewer's prerequisite: split admit vs query and track in-flight probes.

## State machine: Closed → Open → Half-Open → Closed/Open

| State | `isAvailable()` | `admit()` | On success | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Closed** (`!paused()`) | true | true (no-op) | — | `markFailed` arms Open (defect A: fresh pause only) |
| **Open** (`paused()`, `now < resume_time`) | false | one probe per `probe_interval_` (in-flight gated) | `markRecovered` → Closed | `markFailed` no-op (was paused) |
| **expired-Open** (`paused()`, `now >= resume_time`) | false | transition to Half-Open, one trial | `markRecovered` → Closed | `markFailed` escalates `*= 2`, re-arms Open |
| **Half-Open** (`paused()`, `half_open`) | false | false (trial in flight) | `markRecovered` → Closed, backoff reset | `markFailed` escalates `*= 2`, re-arms Open |

`resume_time` stays armed through Half-Open so `paused()` stays true. **Escalation happens only on a probe/trial failure, never on clock expiry** — this removes the "expiry fully reopens" path that slammed a still-dead peer with every slice and re-triggered the storm at 30s/60s/120s.

## The split

`available()` conflated query and admit. Split:
- `isAvailable(l, r) const` — pure predicate (`!paused()`). No mutation, no `updateBestMapping` → recursion gone. Used by `updateBestMapping` and queries.
- `admit(l, r)` — the only mutating admit. Closed → true; Open → one probe per `probe_interval_` (in-flight gated); expired-Open → Half-Open trial; Half-Open → false.
- `cancelProbe(l, r)` — clears an armed probe/trial on a pre-wire failure (see below).

## In-flight tracking

`admit()` arms `probe_in_flight` at selection, but selection ≠ posting. A slice that arms a probe then never reaches the wire orphans the flag and strands the rail. Three paths, all handled:

1. **GDR-exclusion after admit** (`selectFallbackDevice`): GDR check moved **before** `admit`, so a probe is never armed on a GDR-excluded pair.
2. **getEndpoint-null re-queue** (`asyncPostSend`): `cancelProbe` before `submitFromTick`.
3. **HW-reject re-queue** (`asyncPostSend`): `cancelProbe` before `submitFromTick`.

`cancelProbe` clears `probe_in_flight` and reverts `half_open` to expired-Open. No-op when no probe is in flight (normal transfers), so callers invoke it unconditionally on re-queue. Single-threaded per-worker ownership (`WorkerContext::rails[machine_id]` is one `RailMonitor` on one worker thread) makes a `bool` sufficient.

## Out of scope

- **Store-kill**: a probe still hits the dead old port until master drops the old segment (~51s). That is master-side `unmount_expired_mem_segment` / stable segment names, not RailMonitor backoff. Half-Open only stops expiry from re-flooding the dead port; a fresh replica is reached within one `probe_interval` of a successful trial.

## Tests (`tent/tests/rail_monitor_test.cpp`):
- `BurstFailuresDoNotEscalateCooldown` (probing disabled): 8× `markFailed`; `admit()`=true at 1.5s (cooldown stayed 1s), false if escalated to 256s.
- `TrialFailureEscalatesCooldown` (probing disabled): trial fail → 1→2s; 2s expires → trial.
- `TrialSuccessResetsBackoff` (probing disabled): trial success → Closed; next pause uses 1s, not 2s.
- `ExpiryAdmitsOneTrialNotFullReopen` (probing disabled): expiry `admit()`=true, next `admit()`=false (in-flight).
- `InFlightProbeBlocksSecondAdmit` (**default** `probe_interval=1s`): `admit()`=true (probe), `admit()`=false (in-flight), `markRecovered` clears → new probe arms. Exercises in-flight directly, not hidden by `probe_interval=60`.
- `CancelProbeRevertsArmedTrial`: trial armed → `cancelProbe` → re-admits; no-op on Closed.

10 baseline tests renamed `available()`→`isAvailable()`; `CooldownDoesNotCarryOverAfterRecovery` adapted (final expiry assertion → `admit()` with probing disabled).

Probing-disabled tests use `probe_interval=60` so a *cooling* rail's `admit()`=false while an *expired* rail's `admit()`=true — discriminating cooldown **duration**. `InFlightProbeBlocksSecondAdmit` uses the default 1s to test in-flight directly.

title: [Store] Release offload tasks for unreported batch keys
body:
## Description

Fixes #4097. A successful `BatchOffload` can omit duplicate keys (or individual failed file writes) from its completion callback. Those keys remain in `all_bucket_keys`, so the existing sweep never NACKs them and the Master retains their offload tasks and source-replica references until timeout.

Record the keys successfully reported by each completion callback and send the existing `data_size=-1` NACK for the remaining inputs after a successful batch. This releases their tasks without fabricating disk replicas. Existing batch-error handling, storage commits, rollback behavior, RPCs and disk formats are unchanged.

Related work: #3009 handles tasks deferred during bucket grouping; this change handles keys already passed to `BatchOffload` but omitted from its completion callback. #3226 parallelizes per-bucket execution and currently retains the same notification gap; this focused fix may need to be carried into its extracted bucket worker when the two changes are integrated.

title: [Store] Fail-fast when LOCAL_DISK storage_path is shared; salt bucket id + O_EXCL
body:
## Summary
Fixes silent L3 corruption when multiple clients share one `storage_path` ([#3528](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/3528)).

Aligns with maintainer guidance (standalone / **one client per `storage_path`**) plus the independent hardenings called out on the issue:

1. **Fail-fast** — exclusive flock on `{storage_path}/.mooncake_local_disk.lock` in `BucketStorageBackend::Init`
2. **Salt** — `BucketIdGenerator` mixes `getpid()` into the low bits so same-second clients do not share a sequence
3. **`O_EXCL`** — new bucket/meta opens no longer use silent `O_TRUNC`

Does **not** implement layout-independent `owner_id` (RFC option B).

## Description

Add IPv6 bind support for the Mooncake master RPC and HTTP metadata servers. Previously, both servers implicitly bound to IPv4-only (`0.0.0.0`) because no host address was passed to the underlying `coro_http_server`. title: [Store] fix: reset MasterMetricManager on MasterService recreation in HA mode
body:
## Description

Fixes #2210.

In HA mode, `MasterService` is destroyed and recreated on every etcd reconnect / leader transition, but `MasterMetricManager` is a process-level singleton that outlives those transitions. The destructor of the old `MasterService` does not clear the singleton, so values registered during the previous term remain. When the new `MasterService` runs its restore path and calls `inc_*` on top of those stale values, gauges double-count and per-term counters silently accumulate across leader terms.

This PR adds `MasterMetricManager::ResetTermScopedMetrics()` and calls it at the very top of the `MasterService` constructor, before `RestoreState()` or any `inc_*` runs. The new instance starts from a clean baseline and restore re-populates gauges with the actual current state.

Non-HA mode is unaffected: `MasterService` is constructed exactly once, metrics are already 0, so the reset call is a safe no-op.

### Relation to #1186

#1186 raises the same singleton-lifecycle root cause but in more general terms, and it leaves open whether counters should be cleared or synced across leader terms. This PR's scope is just the gauge-class symptom (active_clients, mem/file cache nums, capacities, soft-pin count). The reset helper also clears per-term counters as the simpler default, but that choice is not load-bearing for the bug being fixed here and can be revisited if the project prefers the sync-to-follower alternative.

title: [TransferEngine] Recover auto GID after data-path retry exhaustion
body:
## Description

Fix classic RDMA auto-GID recovery when a GID can reach RTR but repeatedly
fails on the data path with `IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR`.

The existing retry path could rebuild an endpoint while selecting the same
ranked GID again. This change tracks failures by peer connection identity and
uses a bounded recovery sequence:

1. Retry the current GID once with a fresh endpoint/QP.
2. If a distinct fresh endpoint also fails, coordinate the next ranked GID
   with the peer and rebuild the connection.
3. Continue through the ranked candidates (for example, GID 5 -> 7 -> 3)
   until the configured limit is reached.

Any successful data completion clears the failure streak, so a temporarily
unavailable GID is retained when the fresh-QP retry succeeds. After a fallback
connection succeeds, the selected GID remains in use; no background probing of
earlier GIDs is scheduled.

The negotiated `auto_gid_rank` handshake field keeps both peers on the same
candidate. Its presence is optional for compatibility with older peers, and an
explicit `MC_GID_INDEX` continues to bypass automatic selection. The maximum
fallback rank is controlled by `MC_AUTO_GID_MAX_RETRIES` (default: 2; set to 0
to disable auto-GID fallback).

title: [Bugfix][P2P-Store] Validate sizeList against the stored payload layout in GetReplica
body:
## Description

`GetReplica` only checked that `addrList` and `sizeList` had the same non-zero length. It never compared `sizeList` with the layout stored in etcd for the payload, but `doGetReplica` and `updatePayloadMetadata` walk the caller's sizes in `MaxShardSize` steps and index `payload.Shards` by position, transferring the **stored** shard length into each address.

With a mismatched `sizeList` this meant:
- more bytes than stored: `payload.Shards[taskID]` runs past the slice and the process panics;
- a buffer shorter than a shard: the full stored shard length is written past the buffer's end (a plain out-of-bounds write on TCP; on RDMA it either fails or lands in neighbouring registered memory);
- fewer total bytes than stored: only the first shards are fetched, `GetReplica` returns `nil`, and the node advertises itself as a replica source for a partial copy.

This PR adds `validateReplicaLayout`, which returns `ErrInvalidArgument` unless the caller's `sizeList` matches the stored `SizeList` entry for entry, `MaxShardSize` is non-zero, and the implied shard count equals `len(payload.Shards)`. `GetReplica` calls it right after the first metadata read, before any memory is registered. `updatePayloadMetadata` calls it after re-reading the payload on a CAS miss, since that path walks the shard list the same way.

Fixes #4303

Each case asserts `ErrInvalidArgument`, that no memory was registered, and that no metadata update was issued.

title: [Bugfix][Python] Preserve TENT failure decisions in synchronous transfers
body:
## Description

When a TENT WRITE reaches the peer but its acknowledgement is lost, the Python synchronous wrapper submits the request again in a new batch. This discards TENT's non-replayable failure state: both the scalar and batch APIs can write twice and report success after the second attempt.

Let TENT own retry/failover by limiting the wrapper to one submission in TENT mode. Classic TE keeps its existing retry count. Add a loopback regression that forwards a real HP TCP WRITE to a real target, verifies its completion response, and then drops the first ACK. Run it in the CPU-only TENT CI leg.

Refs #3995 (the retry part of P1-sync-status). #4191 addresses asynchronous batch ownership; this change addresses synchronous re-submission. Cancellation handling and stale-handle eviction are outside this change. No new retry mechanism or configuration is added.

## Module

- [x] CI/CD

## Type of Change

title: [Store] Scan a standby remount under the shared snapshot lock
body:
## Description

After an HA promotion, `ReMountSegment` walks all 1024 metadata shards to find the replicas that survived on a standby-restored segment, and until now it did that holding `snapshot_mutex_` exclusively, from the first validation to the last replica. Every data-plane operation on the master waits for the whole walk, which is seconds on a store with a few million objects, and concurrent remounts run one after another. This is the snapshot-lock half of the join-storm stall described in #3937 and RFC #4181 (scenario S1).

### What changes

**Two stages.** `ReMountSegment` now prepares under the shared lock and commits under the exclusive one:

- `PrepareRemount` (shared): validates the request, scans the shards for surviving replicas and rebuilds each segment's allocator from the regions they occupy. None of this mutates anything, so it only blocks the snapshot fork.
- `CommitRemount` (exclusive): mounts the segment, swaps in the rebuilt allocator, re-points the replicas by key and ends the orphan. Its critical section is bounded by the number of replicas on the segment, not by the size of the store.

Splitting the operation lets the scan's findings go stale, which the commit stage handles:

- A replica can disappear between the stages, so the scan records its key rather than a `Replica*`; the commit stage looks the key up again and re-matches the replica against the region of the buffer imported for it. A buffer nobody claims is dropped while the exclusive lock still covers the allocator its region returns to.
- An HA restore can rewrite the state the scan read. A generation counter, advanced by every restore, is compared across the gap; a remount that loses the race returns `UNAVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_STATUS` and the client retries.
- The allocator a mount creates treats the whole segment as free, so the mount and the swap to the rebuilt allocator happen inside one segment-manager critical section.

**`OrphanedSegments`** (`include/ha/orphaned_segments.h`). What an HA restore leaves behind for such segments — the segment list, the bytes still charged to them, the allocators keeping their buffers alive and which endpoints are unreadable — was four `MasterService` members keyed three different ways, stitched together by callers. It is now one record per segment, and the interface follows the segment's lifecycle: `Reset` on restore, `Find` while preparing a remount, `Adopt` when committing it, `IsUnreadable` for readers, `ReleaseAll` on shutdown. `Reset` is the only way to install orphans and always advances the generation, so the check the commit stage depends on cannot be skipped by a future restore path.

**Behavior change: allocated-memory metrics.** Adopting a segment now releases everything still charged to it. Before, only the bytes of the replicas the remount found were released, so the bytes of replicas that died while their segment was orphaned stayed on that segment's allocated-memory metric until the next restore or shutdown, and the leftover entry sent later remounts of the segment through the full scan again. The re-adopted allocator already counts the surviving replicas itself (`OffsetBufferAllocator::Restore`, `CachelibBufferAllocator::adoptImportedBuffer`).

Smaller changes:

- The placeholder allocators a restore creates for NoF replicas are kept in their own member instead of the memory-segment keepalive map, since no memory remount adopts them.
- The scan no longer copies the buffer descriptor of every memory replica in the store, only of those on the segments being re-adopted.
- The restore log line reports `unreadable_segments=<n>` (a segment count) instead of `invalid_endpoints=<n>` (an alias count).

### Relation to open work

- **RFC #4181 / #4180 / #4183.** #4180 takes `client_mutex_` off this path and #4183 moves `Ping` onto its own RPC server; this PR shortens the `snapshot_mutex_` hold. Neither alone stops the mass expiry. This is meant to land before #4180, which will rebase onto it.
- **#3858** separates restored NoF placeholders from the memory-segment keepalive for the same reason as here, and additionally quarantines NoF endpoints. Whichever lands second folds `restored_nof_allocators_` and `standby_nof_allocator_keepalive_` into one; the NoF quarantine stays outside `OrphanedSegments`, which only tracks memory segments awaiting a remount.
- **#3666** changes `ReMountSegment`'s signature for a different purpose; the two will conflict textually in the same function.

### Size

+586/−315 lines outside tests. Most of the `master_service.cpp` churn is the existing `ReMountSegment` body moving into the stage helpers (net +271 in that file); the design context is in RFC #4181 and in this description. It merges cleanly with `main` at e88aacf2.

title: [Store] add dfs capacity metrics
body:
## Description

 Adds observability for the DFS space allocator by exposing three new master metrics: total capacity, allocated bytes, and backing-file count. Previously the DFS allocator had no metrics — `GetTotalCapacity()`/`GetUsedBytes()` were effectively dead code and shard count was only reachable via an ad-hoc admin HTTP endpoint. These metrics support both allocator modes:
- **shard mode** (`DfsGlobalAllocator`, default)
- **bucket mode** (`ImmutableBucketAllocator`)

New metrics:

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `master_dfs_total_capacity_bytes` | Total DFS allocator capacity |
| `master_dfs_allocated_bytes` | Bytes currently allocated by the DFS allocator |
| `master_dfs_file_count` | Number of DFS backing files — shard files in shard mode, immutable bucket files in bucket mode |

Implementation notes:
- Added a mode-agnostic `GetFileCount()` to `DfsAllocatorInterface` so both allocators report through the same interface pointer. The name is deliberately generic ("file count") rather than "shard count" to stay accurate in bucket mode.
- Extended `TieredStorageUsageSnapshot` with a `DfsUsageSnapshot`, populated in`MasterService::GetStorageUsageSnapshot()` and projected into gauges via the existing `project_storage_usage()` path — no new threads or polling.
- Metrics are emitted both on the Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint (`serialize_metrics()`) and in the periodic human-readable admin log (`get_summary_string()`), where a `DFS: <allocated> / <capacity> (pct%) files=N` segment is appended after `SSD Storage`. The segment is omitted when DFS is disabled, so existing deployments' logs are unchanged.

These are distinct from the pre-existing `master_total_file_capacity_bytes` / `master_allocated_file_size_bytes` gauges, which track the 3fs/nfs disk-replica subsystem, not the DFS allocator.

title: [Bugfix][Build] Guard Store hugepage support for macOS (#3926)
body:
## Description

Fixes #3926.

The Store build included Linux-only hugepage headers from a public header. That breaks macOS compilation for every translation unit including client_buffer_allocation.h.

The original revision also moved get_hugepage_size_from_env() into the header, which introduced missing declaration dependencies and left a second definition in the .cpp; this caused the Linux CTest, wheel, CUDA/ROCm/EFA, and TENT CI failures.

## Fix

- Guard Linux hugepage headers and fallback constants with __linux__.
- Keep get_hugepage_size_from_env() declared in the header and implemented once in the .cpp.
- On non-Linux platforms, preserve the requested allocation size, leave hugepage flags unchanged, and log a warning.
- Add the Transfer Engine include directory before Store targets are created when WITH_STORE=ON and WITH_TE=OFF.

The earlier #3894 TCP header change has been removed. Current Apple SDKs include infiniband/verbs.h, and a complete macOS TCP-only Transfer Engine wheel requires broader CMake, linking, and packaging work outside this focused Store fix.

## Why macOS

The goal is to restore the Mooncake Store build and local Store development path reported in #3926. This PR does not claim full macOS support for every Transfer Engine transport.

## Testing

- clang-format-20 --dry-run --Werror passes for the changed C++ files.
- git diff --check passes.
- A header smoke compile passes through both Linux and non-Linux preprocessor paths; only the unrelated CacheLib Slab type is stubbed.
- On a B200 GPU pod, a default WITH_TE=ON, WITH_STORE=ON, USE_CUDA=OFF production build completes 226/226 targets.
- A WITH_TE=OFF Store build compiles the Store source objects past the prior common.h failure; final linking in that mode requires the external libtransfer_engine that WITH_TE=OFF is designed to consume.

title: [TENT] Route RDMA slices by QP pool
body:
## Description

This PR fixes RDMA QP-pool routing so slices that request different `qp_pool`s are posted to the correct pool-specific QPs and therefore use the intended link-layer QoS parameters.

The change does three things:

1. Resolves per-QP link-layer QoS from the owning QP pool, so different pools can use different `service_level` / `traffic_class` values.
2. Routes slices to the worker that owns the QP selected for their requested pool.
3. Splits mixed-pool batches before `submitSlices()`, so a batch containing multiple `qp_pool`s does not inherit the first slice's pool.

For the traditional/default case where no QP pools are configured, the worker keeps the legacy single-submit path. The only added work on that path is checking whether QP-pool routing is enabled.

title: [Reshard] Add Transfer Engine execution and completion lifecycle
body:
## Description

This PR adds the resource-neutral Transfer Engine execution and completion
foundation used by heterogeneous resharding.

It extends the native Scatter transfer path with completion tickets for both
read and write operations. A ticket distinguishes completed transfers,
drained failures, and completion-unknown outcomes. The TENT path also preserves
completion ownership when transfer tasks are merged.

The Reshard layer introduces backend-facing transfer batch contracts,
registration leases, completion fencing, pending-operation ownership,
restart-required quarantine, and a scoped `TransferSubmission` API. Resources
and registrations are released only after a terminal outcome is known. An
unknown outcome remains fenced so callers cannot reuse or free affected memory
prematurely.

This layer is resource-neutral. Model-weight validation, N-D lowering,
Reader/Sink adapters, Store persistence, and framework integration are handled
by later PRs.

Related RFC: #3111

title: feat(te): support per-request RDMA NIC hints
body:
## Description

Add an advisory per-request local RNIC hint to the classic RDMA transport.

Mooncake already had `Topology::selectDevice(location, hint, retry_count)`, but
classic RDMA requests could not pass a non-empty hint to it. This change wires a
new `TransferRequest::nic_hint` through the request-level and per-slice fallback
selection paths.

The hint is intentionally advisory:

- empty hint preserves the existing topology-based selection behavior;
- unknown or disabled devices fall back to normal selection;
- only the initial attempt is pinned, so retries can fail over to another RNIC.

The Python transfer APIs expose the same option as a trailing `nic_hint=""`
keyword argument, without changing existing positional calls. The
`transfer_engine_bench` example exposes `--nic_hint` for hardware validation.

This enables callers that know more than the transport about workload placement
to isolate KV traffic from NCCL/EP traffic or enforce a known GPU–NIC affinity.

title: [Bugfix][TransferEngine] Register HIP IPC memory at allocation granularity
body:
## Description

Fixes #3546.

`hipIpcGetMemHandle` always exports the entire `hipMalloc` allocation, but the
HIP IPC registration path recorded the caller's sub-range address as the buffer
base. The reader's relocation (`dest_addr - entry.addr + shm_addr`) therefore
collapsed every sub-range onto the allocation base, and each buffer silently
returned the first buffer's bytes with `rc=0`. Framework caching allocators
sub-allocate constantly, so any caller registering individual tensors out of one
allocation is affected — including `batch_register_memory`, which loops over the
same function.

The CUDA IPC paths had exactly this bug and it was fixed by registering the
allocation base instead of the requested range — #1622 for
`intranode_nvlink_transport` and #1831 for TENT. The HIP port was missed: its only
`hipMemGetAddressRange` calls are in the fabric-memory branch and in the free
logic, never in the IPC branch. This applies the same fix there: resolve the real
base with `hipMemGetAddressRange`, skip allocations already exported, take the IPC
handle for the base, record the whole allocation in `BufferDesc`, and key
unregistration off that base as well, matching
`IntraNodeNvlinkTransport::registerLocalMemory` and `unregisterLocalMemory`.

title: [Bugfix][Store] Keep scanning for a local MEMORY replica past a local NoF one
body:
## Description

`SelectBestReplica` documents the priority local MEMORY > local NOF_SSD > remote MEMORY > remote NOF_SSD, and its comments note twice that the master may return replicas in any order so the scan must not stop early. The scan did stop early. The first COMPLETE local NOF_SSD replica was returned as soon as it was seen, so a local MEMORY replica sitting later in the list was never examined and the read went over NVMe-over-Fabrics instead of local host memory.

The result depends only on the order the master happened to return, which makes it easy to miss. With the memory replica listed first the selection is correct, with the NoF replica first it is not.

The fix remembers the first local NOF_SSD replica and keeps scanning. It is returned after the loop, so it still outranks every remote replica and the rest of the policy is unchanged.

## Module
- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

## How Has This Been Tested?

Three cases added to `replica_selection_test.cpp`. `LocalMemoryWinsOverEarlierLocalNoF` fails on main and passes with this change. The other two pin behavior the fix must not break, so they pass either way. A local MEMORY replica that is not COMPLETE still falls back to the local NoF one, and a local NoF replica still beats a remote MEMORY one.

title: [Store] Prefetch SSD-only objects to DRAM on exist
body:
**Title**: `[Store] Prefetch SSD-only objects to DRAM on exist`

## Description

With SSD offload enabled, a key whose MEMORY replica has been evicted keeps serving reads from a `LOCAL_DISK` replica — paid synchronously on the get() critical path. For workloads that probe with `exist` before reading (prefix cache lookup, async scheduling), the probe is a strong, early "will read soon" signal.

This PR adds an **opt-in, best-effort** prefetch: `is_exist` / `batch_is_exist` with `ExistOptions.prefetch_to_memory=true` starts an asynchronous SSD→DRAM promotion for keys that turn out SSD-only, so the follow-up `get()` can be served from DRAM. Promotion happens inside the probe→get queueing window; if it does not finish in time, or fails, or DRAM is saturated, behavior degrades to exactly today's SSD read. No correctness contract changes anywhere.

Mechanism, briefly:

- The exist path does a per-key dedup lookup and a thread-pool enqueue only — no RPC added to the probe (a sharded `PrefetchThrottle` with TTL dedup and a DRAM-saturation cooldown).
- A bounded pool (4 threads) classifies candidates via read-only admin replica queries (no lease, no promotion-on-hit, no metrics side effects), then promotes local keys via a new `RegisterPrefetchTask` master RPC plus the **same execution chain promotion-on-hit uses** (`PromotionAllocStart → AllocateBatch → BatchLoad → PromotionWrite → NotifyPromotionSuccess`, extracted as a shared helper), or delegates to remote holders through a new additive `prefetch_offload_object` RPC.
- `RegisterPrefetchTask` is tenant-aware, holder-checked (`holder_id == client_id`), shares the `promotion_in_flight_` cap and the per-key `promotion_tasks` entry with promotion-on-hit (double promotion is impossible), and reports `PROMOTION_ALREADY_EXISTS` distinctly so best-effort callers skip quietly. `NotifyPromotionSuccess` grants the usual read lease for prefetch promotions so the DRAM replica survives until the follow-up get().
- With `ssd_get_wait_ms > 0` (default 0 = off), a batch get headed for SSD gets one demand-side promotion attempt for its disk keys (`ignore_cooldown` bypasses only the client-side throttle backoff — never a master-side gate: the shared in-flight cap, holder check, and dedup TTL all still apply). The get then waits, within **one deadline shared by the whole batch**, for promotions already in flight — and only while a local promotion is actually `kInFlight`/`kCompleted`.

Default configuration is a complete no-op: `enable_ssd_prefetch=false`, `ssd_get_wait_ms=0`.

## Relationship to prior work

- RFC: **#2213** (@Pz1116). The API shape (`ExistOptions` struct rather than a bare bool) follows @LujhCoconut's suggestion on that RFC and the `ReplicateConfig` pattern.
- This PR builds on the design pioneered by **#2646** (@huangdong2022) and presents a new implementation on current main, shaped by the community's feedback on that PR (core commits credit huangdong2022 as co-author). Beyond a clean rebase, this version:
  - shares the promotion execution chain with promotion-on-hit instead of duplicating it (one chain, one failure-handling posture);
  - makes zero wire-protocol changes to existing RPCs (read-only queries ride the pre-existing admin RPCs; new RPCs are purely additive);
  - addresses the review findings on #2646 (throttle entries expiring while in-flight; per-key get-side master polling; missing completion callbacks; tenant handling in task registration);
  - ships a test plan that covers the feature end to end: unit tests for the throttle state machine and the master RPC semantics, a Python integration test with a negative control (plain `exist` must not promote) wired into `scripts/ci/run_ssd_offload_smoke.sh` with its own master instance (`promotion_on_hit=false` so the control is meaningful), and a reproducible A/B benchmark methodology.
- **RFC #3417** (@LujhCoconut): see the alignment discussion there. This PR's mechanism layer (task registration, shared chain, dedup, lease, holder-local execution) is what #3417's router-side explicit trigger would also build on; the exist-probe trigger is the RFC's "engine SDK without a router" path. We deliberately skip the frequency sketch (an explicit probe *is* the hotness signal) and the watermark gate in favor of a DRAM-saturation cooldown that yields to eviction/offload; promotion_in_flight quota is shared, not bypassed. A dedicated prefetch buffer / soft partition is left as follow-up.

## Measured impact

DSv4-Flash + vllm-ascend on Ascend A2; 48 long prefixes (at the prefix-cache hit granularity); fill → overflow-to-SSD → settle → measure; `promotion_on_hit=false`; same dataset and seed across rounds. Absolute latency values are omitted; numbers are TTFT decrease relative to the offload-only baseline of the same round, computed as (baseline − prefetch) / baseline.

**Concurrency 2** (store DRAM comfortably sized):

| metric | TTFT decrease with prefetch |
|---|---:|
| median | **5.2%** |
| mean | **5.1%** |
| p99 | **22.0%** |

**Concurrency 4** (deliberately DRAM-constrained store, ~97.5% full — a
stress regime where eviction churns constantly):

| metric | TTFT decrease with prefetch |
|---|---:|
| median | **85.2%** |
| mean | **81.4%** |
| p99 | **44.9%** |

**NVIDIA H20**:

| metric | TTFT decrease with prefetch |
|---|---:|
| median | **27.4%** |
| mean | **6.7%** |
| p99 | **0.3%** |

Why the rounds differ so much: without prefetch, a queued request pays serial SSD reads on the critical path, so the offload-only baseline's TTFT degrades roughly linearly with queue depth, while the prefetch round hides those reads inside the queueing window and stays flat. The decrease scales with queue depth and with the SSD-read share of TTFT; an idle, serial workload sees ≈ 0 decrease by design.

Honest stress metric from the DRAM-constrained run: promotion **completed 503, failed 860** (DRAM saturation), and the memory-pressure cooldown correctly yielded ~2.1k times — prefetch never starves eviction; it just loses.

## Design

Full component-level design with diagrams: `docs/source/design/ssd-prefetch.md` (in this PR) and design RFC **#4271**.

## Commit-by-commit guide

1. `[Store] Add read-only replica list queries on the client` — registers the pre-existing admin read-only RPCs and adds client wrappers (no lease / no promotion / no metrics).
2. `[Bugfix][Store] Recognize mounted segments in IsReplicaOnLocalMemory` — independent local-memory detection fix (self-contained, could land alone).
3. `[Store] Add PrefetchThrottle for best-effort SSD prefetch` — sharded dedup state machine + cooldown; pure utility, unit-tested.
4. `[Store] Add RegisterPrefetchTask master RPC and prefetch lease` — master side: tenant-aware, holder-checked, quota-shared, distinct idempotency, `from_prefetch` lease. Unit-tested.
5. `[Store] Add FileStorage::PrefetchKeys sharing the promotion execution chain` — extracts `PromoteOneKeyFromLocalDisk` (promotion-on-hit behavior unchanged; its per-key loop body moves verbatim into the helper) and adds the best-effort batch driver.
6. `[Store] Wire SSD prefetch into exist/get paths` — SsdPrefetcher, exist trigger, get-side single-deadline wait, holder RPC.
7. `[Store] Expose ExistOptions in C and Python bindings` — store_c, store_py (keyword args), DummyClient (accepted, ignored with a log).
8. `[Store][CI] Add prefetch-on-exist integration test` — Python integration test wired into `scripts/ci/run_ssd_offload_smoke.sh`.
9. `[Docs][Store] Expand SSD prefetch design doc with component-level design` — full component-level design with diagrams (`docs/source/design/ssd-prefetch.md`).
10. `[Docs][Store] Fix mermaid syntax in SSD prefetch design diagrams` — diagram rendering fixes, docs only.
11. `[Store] Apply clang-format and ruff-format to prefetch changes` — mechanical formatting, no behavior change.

## Rolling-upgrade compatibility

- No existing RPC signature changes.
- New RPCs (`RegisterPrefetchTask`, `prefetch_offload_object`) are additive: old masters/peers reject them and prefetch degrades to a no-op.
- Read-only queries reuse the pre-existing admin RPC handlers.
- All knobs default off: `enable_ssd_prefetch=false`, `ssd_get_wait_ms=0`.

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Test commands:**
```bash
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R \
  'prefetch_throttle_test|prefetch_task_master_test|client_readonly_query_test|promotion_on_hit_test|file_storage_promotion_test'
bash scripts/ci/run_ssd_offload_smoke.sh   # includes test_prefetch_on_exist.py
```
Manual end-to-end: A/B TTFT benchmark on vllm-ascend (fill → overflow → settle → measure; see "Measured impact").

- [x] Integration tests pass (`test_prefetch_on_exist` incl. negative control: plain exist does not promote)
- [x] Manual testing: A/B TTFT above; promotion-on-hit regression tests green (shared execution chain)

title: [Wheel] Support DataProto matrix partial reads
body:
## Description

Add partial matrix reads for dense two-dimensional DataProto `batch` fields.

The public `batch_slices` mapping selects a column slice per field and composes
with the existing `rows` selection. A single M x N implementation covers row
batches, column batches, and general submatrices without separate code paths.

The implementation:

- plans byte ranges from matrix shape, dtype, selected rows, and column slice;
- coalesces consecutive full-width rows;
- uses one BufferPool lease and one `get_into_ranges` call across selected
  fields, DataProto stages, and payload chunks;
- keeps NumPy results writable and rewrites native tensor metadata for the
  sliced shape;
- commits caller destinations only after every selected field and the final
  DataProto result have been constructed successfully;
- falls back to regular materialization when ranged reads are unavailable or
  the request exceeds the range or physical-fragment limits.

The fast path guarantees one batched ranged call. The fallback is intentionally
whole-request and does not guarantee a single backend call; this keeps the
destination commit semantics and the hot path small. Logical ranges are capped
per field, while physical fragments are capped at 4096 across the entire
batched request before BufferPool allocation.

The append write path is unchanged. Dense matrix fields added through
`append_dataproto_fields()` are resolved from their existing stage refs and can
participate in the same batched partial read.

title: [Store][TransferEngine] Guard standalone mains against duplicate glog initialization
body:
## Description

`mooncake_client` crashloops on startup when `MC_LOG_DIR` points to a valid, writable directory (observed on a 0.3.12 source build; glog >= 0.6.0 CHECK-fails with `You called InitGoogleLogging() twice!`).

Order of events:

1. `mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transport/rdma_transport/worker_pool.cpp` evaluates `globalConfig()` from a **static initializer before `main()`**; `loadGlobalConfig()` sees `MC_LOG_DIR`, calls `InitGoogleLogging()`, and — for a valid directory — also sets `FLAGS_log_dir`.
2. `main()` (`real_client_main.cpp`, init added in #1925) then sees a non-empty `FLAGS_log_dir` and calls `InitGoogleLogging()` a second time → CHECK fail.

The guard added in #3727 covers the opposite order (a host program pre-initializes glog before loading mooncake) and cannot help here: in a standalone binary, `loadGlobalConfig()` is the *first* initializer, so the guard lets it through and `main()` still double-initializes. `master.cpp` has the same unguarded pattern (identical crash once `MC_LOG_DIR` is set for the master).

**Fix**: extract the version-conditional "already initialized" check from `config.cpp` into `mooncake-transfer-engine/include/glog_compat.h` as `mooncake::InitGoogleLoggingOnce()`, and use it in both standalone mains and in `config.cpp` — one implementation instead of three diverging copies. A regression test reproduces the static-init-then-main order on top of the existing `glog_preinitialized_test`.

title: [TE] Metadata cache invalidation on rdma failure
body:
## Description

This PR improves Transfer Engine metadata handling for node replacement scenarios.

** Code are fully revised: ** #3837 -> #3072 -> #3944

When an RDMA failure suggests that cached remote metadata may be stale, the worker now triggers metadata cache invalidation. The invalidation keeps existing segment IDs as handles for in-flight retry paths, but marks remote segment descriptors stale and clears cached RPC metadata so the next lookup reloads fresh metadata from the metadata backend.

The change intentionally does not proactively disconnect all cached RDMA endpoints. Existing endpoint failure cleanup remains responsible for the failed endpoint, while metadata refresh is handled lazily on the next lookup.

title: [TransferEngine] Intern SegmentDesc NIC paths for RDMA slice mapping
body:
## Description

RDMA `submitPostSend` currently concatenates `server@nic` into a per-slice
`std::string` on every descriptor. Mapping, batched enqueue, CQ drain, and
redispatch then copy or hash that owned string again.

This change interns those paths in a process-lifetime pool and points
`Slice` at the interned string. Pointers outlive a COW `SegmentDesc`
replacement. Interned paths are rebuilt from `devices` / `name` /
`rdma_server_name` in `addLocalSegment` and `decodeSegmentDesc`, not from
`rebuildBufferRangeIndex()`. `internedNicPath()` falls back to the intern
pool without mutating the snapshot when sizes differ, and logs
`LOG_FIRST_N(WARNING, 8)` on that path. `addLocalSegment` requires exclusive
ownership of `desc`; `allocateLocalSegmentID` copies before mutating. Local
buffer COW publishes only after rebuild. `peerNicPath()` returns the interned path
when set, and falls back to `peer_nic_path` for transports that still
fill the owned string. Batched enqueue uses `peerNicPath()` so an empty
owned string does not send every slice to the same worker.

Measured `submitTransfer` p50 on same-host H20 / `mlx5_bond_0` RDMA (classic
tebench, VRAM, GPU0→GPU1 READ, 4 KiB blocks). First two iterations skipped.
Wait / bandwidth is completion time and is not claimed. Baseline is current
`origin/main` (already includes #4259, #4273, and #4279).

title: [Bugfix][TE] Register direct ACL VMM fabric memory as device
body:
## Description

Fixes the memory type used when registering fabric memory, so that fabric memory mode no longer registers **every** fabric buffer as device memory. Only the buffers that bypass `adxl::MallocMem` - the direct ACL VMM allocations made by `ascend_allocator` - are looked back up at registration time and registered as `MemType::Device`; allocations made through `adxl::MallocMem` keep using `MemType::Host`.

**Background:** the VA of a direct ACL VMM allocation is reported by `aclrtPointerGetAttributes()` as HOST / HOST_NUMA, so it was classified as `MEM_HOST`. With the buffer pool enabled, `registerMem` skips `MEM_HOST` buffers entirely, and the fabric transfer path does not fall back to a local copy, so D2H/H2D transfers fail. An earlier revision registered everything as `MEM_DEVICE` whenever `use_fabric_mem_` was set, which also changed allocations that ADXL owns and exports through its own host-memory path. This PR instead distinguishes allocations by their origin.

**Changes:**

1. `ascend_allocator`: the allocation table (`AllocRecord`) now records the allocation size, and a new `ascend_is_direct_vmm_memory()` looks an address back up in it. The lookup only matches records flagged as direct allocations, so buffers returned by `adxl::MallocMem` (recorded with `is_direct_alloc == false`) can never match. Both insertion points of `AllocRecord` record the length.
2. `AscendDirectTransport::registerLocalMemory()`: when this TE is a fabric TE and the buffer is a direct VMM allocation, `mem_type` is overridden to `adxl::MEM_DEVICE`. The override is one-way (Host -> Device), so explicitly device memory such as `location="npu"` is unaffected. The gate is `use_fabric_mem_` (this TE's own fabric flag) rather than the process-wide config, so a co-located non-fabric TE is not affected.
3. `ascend_allocator`: the direct VMM path now calls `aclrtMemSetAccess` after `aclrtMapMem`, granting the current device read/write access, and rolls back with `Unmap + ReleaseMemAddress + FreePhysical` if the grant fails. `aclrtMapMem` only binds the pages to the host, so the NPU needs this explicit grant; `adxl::MallocMem` does the same for its own allocations.

Per request, this PR contains **no unit test changes**.

## Notes for reviewers

- The lookup matches on the **start address only** and does not require the registered range to be contained in the allocation. A caller may register a longer range than was allocated - a store segment is mounted at its requested size, while best-effort fabric allocation (`align_down_1g` or a percentile step down) can return less. Requiring full containment would silently keep that buffer as `MEM_HOST`, which is exactly the bug this PR fixes, so the lookup would not take effect on the store segment path.
- Related but out of scope: with `split_limit` set, `real_client.cpp` mounts `segment_size` even when `mapped_size` is smaller, so the capacity reported to the master can exceed the memory that was actually mapped (`mapped_size < segment_size`). Worth a separate look; it is not touched here.
- The `location.id` for `aclrtMemSetAccess` must be a driver logical id while `aclrtGetDevice` returns a user id. The conversion follows the existing code in `shared_segment/ascend_shared_segment.cpp`. Deployments that expose only a subset through `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` are worth a confirmation on real hardware.
- The existing mock unit test `ascend_direct_transport_test.cpp` implements its own set of ACL stubs, and the two calls added here (`aclrtGetLogicDevIdByUserDevId`, `aclrtMemSetAccess`) are not stubbed. Per request this PR does not touch test files; if needed later, the stubs are `aclrtGetLogicDevIdByUserDevId` writing back its argument and `aclrtMemSetAccess` returning `ACL_ERROR_NONE`.
  - Impact: that test's `aclrtReserveMemAddress` stub returns a `malloc(64)` pointer rather than a real ACL VMM address. On a machine without an NPU these two real library calls "succeed" spuriously (measured: `aclrtGetLogicDevIdByUserDevId(0) == 0` and `aclrtMemSetAccess(malloc_ptr) == 0`), which is why all 79 tests pass here. On an A3 machine with an NPU, `aclrtMemSetAccess` will likely reject that non-ACL address, the grant returns -1, allocation returns nullptr, and `AgentModeAllocTest.DirectVmmDoesNotRotateSequencer` plus `FabricMemBestEffortAllocTest.*` would fail.

title: [TransferEngine] Recover redis metadata connection after disconnects
body:
## Description

Fixes #4003.

`RedisStoragePlugin` in `mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_metadata_plugin.cpp`
held a single long-lived `redisContext` and never rebuilt it. hiredis latches any
I/O error into the context and rejects every subsequent command, so **one
disconnect permanently disabled metadata publishing and lookup for the rest of the
process lifetime**: `get()` / `set()` / `remove()` returned false forever, segment
registration and lookup failed, and only restarting the process recovered.

We hit this in production with a managed Redis reached through a TCP load balancer
that reclaims connections idle for more than ~4000s. The connection is only touched
on segment (un)registration and on the first lookup of a given remote segment, so it
sits idle for hours; with no TCP keepalive nothing is sent during that window and the
load balancer silently reclaims the socket. Redis itself stayed healthy the whole
time — the broken state lived entirely in the client's cached context, so restarting
Redis did not help.

### What changed

1. **Reconnect and retry once on connection-level failure** (`execLocked`). Only null
   replies are retried: a `REDIS_REPLY_ERROR` means the server answered and rejected
   the command, so retrying cannot help. GET/SET/DEL are idempotent, so the retry is
   safe.
2. **AUTH/SELECT moved into the connect path** so they are replayed on every
   reconnect, and a construction-time failure is no longer terminal. Previously, a
   Redis that was unreachable at startup left `client_` null forever.
3. **Connect timeout, command timeout and TCP keepalive.** There was previously no
   timeout at all, so a slow or blackholed Redis could block the caller indefinitely
   while holding `access_client_mutex_`. The 3s values match the Redis client already
   used by Mooncake Store HA
   (`mooncake-store/src/ha/common/redis/redis_connection.cpp`). Keepalive matters
   because this connection is idle for long stretches, and the command timeout is what
   makes recovery work when a middlebox drops the flow without resetting it.
4. **`getWithStatus()` routed through the same retry path.** #3072 added that override
   so `syncSegmentCache()` can tell an absent key from a backend outage, but it issued
   its own `redisCommand()` with `if (!client_) return kUnavailable;` and no reconnect.
   Rebasing onto current main without touching it would have left #4003 reproducible
   through that entry point, and `syncSegmentCache()` calls it periodically. `get()` now
   delegates to it, which also removes the duplicated GET handling. A null reply after
   `execLocked()` means the backend is unreachable, so it maps to `kUnavailable` and
   never to `kNotFound`, preserving the invariant #3072 added.
5. **CI now executes the Redis regression tests.** The job that runs `ctest` configured
   the tree without `-DUSE_REDIS=ON`, so the suite was compiled but never run; the job
   that enables `USE_REDIS` builds without running `ctest`. Adding the flag is enough —
   `dependencies.sh` already installs `libhiredis-dev` on that runner and the top-level
   `CMakeLists.txt` calls `enable_testing()`.

No public interface changes. `MetadataStoragePlugin::Create()` could already return a
plugin with a dead connection, and no caller inspects connectivity, so behaviour for
callers is unchanged apart from now recovering.

One observable change for operators: `get()` now logs a nil reply at WARNING instead of
ERROR. An absent key is an expected outcome when resolving a segment that is not
registered yet, so the previous level reported a normal lookup miss as an error. The
message text is unchanged (`RedisStoragePlugin: unable to get <key> from <uri>`), so
anything matching on the text still matches, but alerting that keys on ERROR level will
no longer fire for lookup misses. The connection-level failure path — which is what
actually indicates a problem — is unaffected.

## Module

- [x] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)
- [ ] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)
- [ ] Reshard (`mooncake-reshard`)
- [ ] Mooncake EP (`mooncake-ep`)
- [ ] Mooncake PG (`mooncake-pg`)
- [ ] Integration (`mooncake-integration`)
- [ ] P2P Store (`mooncake-p2p-store`)
- [ ] Python Wheel (`mooncake-wheel`)
- [ ] Common (`mooncake-common`)
- [ ] Mooncake RL (`mooncake-rl`)
- [x] CI/CD
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Other

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added `mooncake-transfer-engine/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test.cpp`, which
drives the plugin through the public `MetadataStoragePlugin::Create("redis://...")`
factory against an in-process RESP fake server. A real Redis cannot be scripted to
drop a connection at an exact moment, which is precisely the condition under test, and
the fake keeps the test hermetic (no Redis server required in CI).

Cases covered:

- set/get/remove round trip
- `set` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `get` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `getWithStatus` recovers after the server drops the connection
- `getWithStatus` reports `kNotFound` for an absent key while the server is up, and
  `kUnavailable` — never `kNotFound` — once the server is gone
- `remove` recovers after the server drops the connection
- recovery when Redis is unavailable at construction time and comes up later
- AUTH and SELECT are replayed on reconnect
- operations still fail, and fail fast, when Redis stays down

**Test commands:**
```bash
cmake -S mooncake-transfer-engine -B build -G Ninja \
  -DUSE_REDIS=ON -DUSE_HTTP=ON -DUSE_ETCD=OFF -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build -j"$(nproc)" --target transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
./build/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test

# and again under ASan + UBSan
cmake -S mooncake-transfer-engine -B build-asan -G Ninja \
  -DUSE_REDIS=ON -DUSE_HTTP=ON -DUSE_ETCD=OFF -DBUILD_UNIT_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g"
cmake --build build-asan -j"$(nproc)" --target transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
./build-asan/tests/transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test
```

The binary is invoked directly above because `enable_testing()` is only called from the
top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, so a standalone Transfer Engine configure builds the test
target but registers no CTest tests. In CI the suite now runs through `ctest` from the
repository-root configure, because this PR adds `-DUSE_REDIS=ON` to the job that runs
it.

**Test results:**
- [x] Unit tests pass — 9/9, 167 ms total
- [ ] Integration tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing done — see production validation below

```
[==========] Running 9 tests from 1 test suite.
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.SetGetRemoveRoundTrip (0 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.SetSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetWithStatusRecoversAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.GetWithStatusDistinguishesAbsentKeyFromOutage (20 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.RemoveSucceedsAfterServerDropsConnection (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.RecoversWhenRedisIsDownAtConstruction (20 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.AuthAndSelectAreReplayedOnReconnect (21 ms)
[       OK ] RedisStoragePluginTest.FailsWhenRedisStaysDown (20 ms)
[  PASSED  ] 9 tests.
```

The run emits the expected recovery diagnostics, e.g. `RedisStoragePlugin: SET
mooncake/node-1 failed on 127.0.0.1:17885: Server closed the connection;
reconnecting and retrying once`, followed by a successful retry.

The same 9 cases also pass under `-fsanitize=address,undefined` (190 ms, no
sanitizer reports and no LeakSanitizer findings at exit), which covers the
`redisContext` and `redisReply` lifetimes on the reconnect path.

These tests exercise the reconnect path via a peer that closes or refuses the
connection, so they cover the latched-error case rather than the silent-blackhole
case; the command timeout is therefore not exercised by them, which is also why the
whole suite finishes in 167 ms with no stalls.

**Production validation:** the reconnect, timeout and keepalive changes have been
cherry-picked onto v0.3.11.post1 and run for 5 days in a prefill/decode disaggregated
deployment on 8 H800 nodes, against the same managed Redis behind an L4 load balancer
described in #4003, where idle connections are reclaimed after roughly 4000s. Before the
patch the failure was fully deterministic there: SGLang (Store client) was restarted
roughly every 4 hours, and every restart reproduced it. The two intervals are different
things — the load balancer reclaims the connection about 4000s after the last Redis
access, but the dead context is only discovered at the next metadata operation, and a
restart is what forces those segment registrations and lookups to happen. Once
discovered, metadata publishing and lookup stayed broken for the remaining lifetime of
that process. After the patch the same restart cadence has not reproduced it once over
the 5-day run; a reclaimed connection now shows up only as a single warning followed by
a successful retry:

    RedisStoragePlugin: SET mooncake/ram/<segment> failed on <host>:6379: Server closed
    the connection; reconnecting and retrying once

To be precise about what that run covers: the deployed build predates `getWithStatus()`
(added by #3072), so the routing of that entry point through the same retry path is
covered by the unit tests above rather than by the production run.

CI coverage: the job that runs `ctest` previously configured without `-DUSE_REDIS=ON`,
so these tests were compiled but never executed. This PR adds the flag to that job, so
`transfer_metadata_redis_plugin_test` now runs in CI. It needs no Redis server.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have formatted my code using `./scripts/code_format.sh`
- [x] I have run pre-commit on the files changed in this PR and all hooks pass
- [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable) — no user-facing interface
      change; happy to document the timeout values if they should be configurable
- [x] I have added tests to prove my changes are effective
- [ ] For changes >500 LOC: I have filed an RFC issue — non-test changes are ~245
      lines in a single file and this is a bug fix rather than an architectural
      change, so no RFC was filed. Issue #4003 describes the bug.

### Known limitations, called out deliberately

- **No reconnect backoff.** While Redis is unreachable, every operation now attempts a
  fresh connection instead of failing immediately, and it does so while holding
  `access_client_mutex_`. Worst case for a blackholed Redis is roughly command timeout
  plus reconnect plus command timeout. This is still bounded, whereas before this PR
  the same situation could block forever with no timeout at all, but if maintainers
  prefer a cooldown (skip reconnect attempts for N ms after a failure) I am glad to
  add one.
- **SIGPIPE.** Writing to a socket the peer has closed can raise SIGPIPE on Linux, and
  no Mooncake code installs `SIG_IGN`. This exposure is unchanged by this PR — the
  pre-existing code issued the same write on the same dead socket — so it is not
  addressed here, but it seems worth a separate look.
- **`set`/`remove` do not inspect `reply->type`.** A server-level error such as
  `-READONLY` during a failover is still reported as success. This is pre-existing
  behaviour, left untouched to keep the diff focused, and tracked separately as
  requested.

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (specify below)

AI assistance was used for code review, test scaffolding, and drafting this
description. The bug was diagnosed from a production incident on our side. I have
reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the change end-to-end.
