title: [1/3] [TransferEngine] Add HOST_NUMA Fabric allocation core
body:
## Summary

This PR provides the minimum Transfer Engine prerequisite for RFC #2914.

It adds CUDA `HOST_NUMA` Fabric allocation and closes the exact-range NVLink
registration lifecycle. It intentionally does **not** add the Store EGM pool or
the complete Provider/Consumer data path.

## Stack

This is **[1/3]** of the RFC implementation stack:

1. #2966 — HOST_NUMA/Fabric Transfer Engine prerequisite (this PR).
2. #3335 — Provider-owned EGM Store pool.
3. #3431 — direct remote-memory reads into GPU destinations.

The fork branches form this exact commit chain. GitHub still displays each
community PR against `main` because a cross-fork PR cannot use another fork
branch as its base.

## Core changes

### HOST_NUMA placement

- Adds `NvlinkHostNumaAllocation` for Fabric-capable CUDA `HOST_NUMA` memory.
- Validates the IPC switch and every visible GPU's VMM, Fabric, and HOST_NUMA
  VMM capabilities independently from NUMA discovery.
- Auto discovery sorts and deduplicates GPU-local NUMA IDs and validates each
  discovered node's granularity.
- Explicit placement validates only the selected node's granularity, so an
  unrelated node cannot block the override.
- Grants access to all visible GPUs in one batched `cuMemSetAccess` call.

### Retryable exact-range registration lifecycle

- Inserts a handle-free registration placeholder before retaining the CUDA
  allocation handle. A duplicate or map-allocation failure therefore cannot
  leave an untracked retained handle.
- If `cuMemRetainAllocationHandle()` fails, returns `ERR_MEMORY`, removes the
  placeholder, and does not publish metadata.
- Export failure, publication rollback, and public unregister share the same
  lock-held cleanup helper. A failed registration can be retried at the same
  address: pending cleanup finishes before a new handle is acquired, while a
  successful registration still rejects duplicates.
- Registration pins protect the allocation's VA throughout registration,
  rollback, and deferred/batch cleanup. `Release()` refuses to unmap a pinned
  range. A range being released remains unavailable for registration until
  address-free succeeds.
- Batch deletion retains handles and pins until metadata publication succeeds;
  partial cleanup retries skip already completed work.
- Metadata cleanup is recorded before external publication completes, so a
  later retry does not repeat a completed delete. `ERR_ADDRESS_NOT_REGISTERED`
  remains idempotent.
- A failed `cuMemRelease()` preserves the registration record and handle
  ownership; a later unregister retries only the remaining release stage.
- Allocation-owned release follows the same rule: ownership is cleared only
  after a successful release, and a failed call can be retried.
- Every rollback checks the release result instead of silently discarding it.
- `Create()` requires an empty output. An error may still return a partial
  owner; the caller must retain it and retry `Release()`. Destruction remains
  best-effort, not a replacement for successful explicit cleanup.

CUDA documents that these APIs may report errors from earlier asynchronous
work and does not explicitly guarantee failure atomicity. This PR deliberately
treats a non-successful release as retaining ownership so cleanup remains
retryable. That policy and its accepted ambiguity are documented in the code.
See the [CUDA Driver API virtual-memory documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__VA.html).

### Lifetime and tests

- Makes `OwnedRangeRegistry` a process-lifetime heap singleton to avoid static
  destruction-order hazards.
- Adds hardware-free scripted coverage for capability/placement failures,
  retain/export/publication failures, metadata retry, idempotent unregister,
  release retry, concurrent register/release, VA reuse, and partial batch cleanup.

### CI integration

- Runs the two fake-driver CTest entries in the existing `unit-tests` build
  with `USE_MNNVL=ON`, reusing the CUDA driver runtime setup.
- Removes the separate NVLink build and its path filter.
- Labels the real GPU entry `nvlink_gpu` and excludes only that entry from the
  CPU runner. Hardware and fake-driver cases use separate `GTEST_FILTER`
  environments, so they do not run twice.
- Adds an optional label exclusion to the shared CTest action. Nightly keeps
  its existing test selection when the input is omitted.

## Scope boundary

This PR does not change Store behavior, Consumer mapping/cache, wire schema,
`TransferMetadata` behavior, RDMA behavior, or Store configuration. Store EGM pooling,
the full Provider/Consumer path, and GB200/NVL72 integration validation belong
to the follow-up Store layer. GB200 validation is therefore not a merge gate
for #2966.

## Review size

- 1 logical commit.
- 12 changed files.
- +2,570/-2 lines.

## Validation

This revision consolidates the CI build and test selection; allocation,
registration, transfer, and cleanup behavior are unchanged.

- [x] clang-format 20 check on PR-changed C/C++ lines.
- [x] `git diff --check` and all applicable touched-file pre-commit hooks.
- [x] CUDA 12.8 ARM64 focused build.
- [x] `nvlink_vmm_unit` (2 tests).
- [x] CUDA-off Transfer Engine build.
- [x] CI shell-script regressions (12 tests, including 5 new CTest-action tests).
- [x] CTest JSON selection: only the real GPU entry is excluded; both
  fake-driver entries remain selected and ran successfully.
- [x] New-head complete `unit-tests` sweep and GitHub Actions CI Gate.

Local CUDA-on/off regression tests passed on the composed stack (#3431).
GitHub Actions passed the complete CTest sweep (226 entries) and CI Gate
for this revision. Both fake-driver entries ran successfully; the hardware-only
entry was excluded on the CPU runner.

title: [Bugfix][TENT] Replace stale buffers when refreshing segment info
body:
## Description

Reusing a `SegmentInfo` output object with `getSegmentInfo()` appends new buffers to the previous result. Repeated queries duplicate entries, and a refresh after unregistering a buffer still reports that old address.

Clear the output buffer list after acquiring the current segment descriptor, before filling either the memory or file result. This is a one-line runtime fix. Add a regression to the existing local-memory lifecycle test that queries twice into one object, unregisters the buffer, and queries again.

This fixes output-object reuse, not the remote descriptor cache. The existing TENT CI job already runs this test target. No new state, configuration or test target is needed.

title: [TransferEngine] Reuse batch-local transport and single-device RDMA preparation
body:
## Description

#4259 already reuses the last-hit device inside one MR. The first-attempt
`selectDevice` / `selectPeerDevice` still runs for every request in a
submission, including the topology walk, even when the snapshot is a single
HCA with unique, non-overlapping coverage.

This change keeps a function-local cache for that first attempt. Consecutive
requests that stay inside the same buffer reuse `buffer_id` / `device_id`
without calling `selectDevice` again. The cache is not used on retries,
multi-HCA topology, overlapping range indexes, or `segments:` names.

#4273 already reuses `selectTransport` across consecutive same-`target_id`
requests. This PR also gates that reuse on `globalConfig().metacache`, so
`MC_DISABLE_METACACHE=1` still re-runs MultiTransport routing (protocol to
`Transport*`) on every request. It does not restore a per-request RDMA
`SegmentDesc` fetch; `submitTransferTask` still deduplicates by `target_id`.

Measured `submitTransfer` p50 on same-host H20 / `mlx5_bond_0` RDMA (classic
tebench, VRAM, GPU0→GPU1 READ, 4 KiB blocks). First two iterations skipped.
Wait / bandwidth is completion time and is not claimed. Baseline is current
`origin/main` (already includes #4259 and #4273). The cache is inactive on
multi-HCA topology, so these numbers apply to single-HCA hosts.

title: [CI] Publish explicit CUDA flavor tags
body:
## Description

Align Mooncake master image tags with their CUDA flavors.

The previous workflow published CUDA 12 under an unqualified tag and CUDA 13 under a `-cuda13` suffix, making the CUDA flavor ambiguous. This change publishes symmetric fixed-version tags and makes CUDA 13 the default flavor.

- Publish `<version>-cuda12` for CUDA 12.
- Publish `<version>-cuda13` for CUDA 13.
- Make `<version>` alias the CUDA 13 image.
- Add optional floating flavor tags `cuda12` and `cuda13`.
- Make `latest` point to CUDA 13 when floating tags are updated.
- Keep alias promotion after both architecture smoke tests.
- Deprecate `latest-cuda13` in the new naming contract.
- Document the new image tag usage.

## Module

- [ ] Transfer Engine (`mooncake-transfer-engine`)
- [ ] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)
- [ ] Mooncake Conductor (`mooncake-conductor`)
- [ ] Reshard (`mooncake-reshard`)

title: [Bugfix][Store] Preserve tenant in BatchReplicaClear RPC
body:
## Description

`MasterClient::BatchReplicaClear` previously omitted its configured tenant when invoking the RPC. The server wrapper therefore used the default tenant, which could silently leave the requested tenant's replicas untouched and clear same-named replicas in the default tenant instead.

This change:
- carries the client's tenant through the `BatchReplicaClear` RPC;
- resolves and validates that tenant in `WrappedMasterService` before forwarding to the existing tenant-aware service overload;
- preserves default-tenant behavior when tenant quotas are disabled; and
- adds an in-process RPC regression test with the same object key in two tenants.

Fixes #4262.

title: [Bugfix] Handle unavailable target segments in classic tebench
body:
## Description

Fixes #3979.

Classic `tebench` dereferenced a null segment descriptor when
`openSegment()` could not resolve a target. This caused the initiator to
terminate with `SIGSEGV` instead of reporting a startup failure.

This change validates the segment handle, descriptor, and registered buffer
list before starting worker threads. Invalid targets now produce a
target-specific error and `tebench` exits normally with a nonzero status.

The change does not alter transport selection, wire protocols, public APIs, or
benchmark result formats.

The regression test uses real Classic TCP engines and covers an unavailable
target, a target with no registered buffers, retry after a partial multi-target
failure, and a valid WRITE/READ path.

## Reproduction

Run a Classic initiator without starting the specified target:

```bash
MC_FORCE_TCP=1 ./build/issue-3979/mooncake-transfer-engine/benchmark/tebench \
  --backend=classic \
  --xport_type=tcp \
  --metadata_type=p2p \
  --target_seg_name=127.0.0.1:1 \
  --seg_type=DRAM \
  --total_buffer_size=65536
```

Before this change, the initiator terminates with `SIGSEGV`. After this change,
it logs `Failed to open target segment: 127.0.0.1:1` and exits normally with
status 1. See #3979 for the complete reproduction details.

title: [Doc][TENT] Add the deadline scheduling design doc
body:
## Description

Promised in the review of #3907: a design document for the deadline machinery, which until now had no entry of its own. Device selection is documented in `slice-spraying.md`; the admission queue and the RDMA bandwidth arbitration were mentioned only in passing inside its transmit-estimate section, and of the eleven `runtime_queue/*` keys one appeared anywhere in the docs.

`docs/source/design/tent/deadline-scheduling.md` covers, in order: the path a `deadline_ns` takes from `Request` to metric; the shared `DeadlineMlu` predictor and why the two layers read different `bytes_ahead`; the admission queue (capacity limits, EDF insert, slack promotion, deadline-infeasible drop, eligibility, dispatch window and the progress-worker fallback timer, the bandwidth provider); the RDMA arbitration (`orderByDeadline`, posted-bytes queue-ahead, slot-by-slot greedy order within a priority tier); the two bandwidth series and why per-completion timing cannot feed the predictors; a three-way comparison with device selection; every configuration key with type, default and meaning, plus the request fields and C++/Python examples; the two metrics; where each effect is observable (drop and arbitration act on RDMA only); and the known limits (no drop hook installed, no lower bound on the threshold, mixed-submit bypass, quarantined-owner bytes, no RDMA completion wake).

Two small edits alongside: `overview.md` gets a "TENT Deadline Scheduling" toctree entry, and `slice-spraying.md`'s transmit-estimate section links to the new page; one phrase there claimed the arbitration's 64 exactly-resolved slots are "more than one post can take", which is not so with the default `max_qp_wr` of 256, and is corrected. The `deadline_ns` comment in `types.h` still said the field "does not yet drive any admission or scheduling decision"; it now names what reads it and points at the document.

title: Store: add reusable ranged-read snapshots
body:
## Description

Add a reusable ranged-read metadata snapshot for Store reads and use it in the Engram and reconstructed-shard read paths.

The motivation is to reduce TTFT-sized Engram read latency by avoiding repeated Store query/lease metadata work when the same key set is read repeatedly. The actual TransferEngine/RDMA data path is unchanged in this PR.

### API and behavior

- Add `PyClient::RangedReadSnapshot`, a caller-owned snapshot of fresh `batch_query()` results.
- Add `prepare_get_into_ranges_snapshot(keys)` and `refresh_get_into_ranges_snapshot(...)`.
- Add `get_into_ranges_from_snapshot(...)` for reads that must use the supplied snapshot and must not re-query or renew leases.
- Cache one snapshot per `EngramStore` layer and invalidate it on `populate()` and successful `remove_from_store()`.
- Reuse the same snapshot abstraction in the parallel/reconstructed-shard read path when query results are already cached.

Snapshot refresh time is derived from the earliest lease timeout and is set to halfway through the remaining lease window. If any key fails query or has an expired lease, the snapshot is not treated as reusable. Ordinary `get_into_ranges` keeps the existing query-refresh behavior.

title: [Store] Read a batch's LOCAL_DISK endpoints in parallel
body:
## Description

We run SSD offload in production. A single batch's LOCAL_DISK replicas routinely
live on several offload endpoints rather than on one peer.

The client already groups such a batch by transport endpoint, but then reads the
groups one endpoint at a time:

```cpp
for (auto &[endpoint, objects] : offload_objects) {
    auto read_result = batch_get_into_offload_object_internal(endpoint, objects);
    ...
}
```

The groups are independent — different peers, different disks, different RPCs — so
the batch ends up waiting for the *sum* of the per-endpoint latencies instead of the
slowest one. Every extra peer a batch spans adds its full read to the total, and the
effect gets worse exactly as the cluster gets bigger. The client thread spends that
whole time blocked on `syncAwait`, not on CPU.

This PR reads the endpoints concurrently instead.

### Commits

**1. `[Store] Add ParallelExecute, a pool-backed bounded fan-out helper`**

`ParallelExecute(items, task, pool)` runs independent items on a persistent
`ThreadPool` the caller owns and returns one result per item **in input order**, so
the caller's existing merge loop needs no change at all. Design points worth a
comment:

- **All but the last item are dispatched; the last runs inline on the caller thread.**
  This keeps a single-item call off the pool entirely, and guarantees progress even
  when every worker is busy with something else.
- **A pool that cannot accept work degrades to serial execution** rather than
  failing — e.g. a pool already stopped during teardown. Correctness does not depend
  on the pool being alive.
- **A throwing task is reported as `INTERNAL_ERROR` for that item only.** Letting an
  exception escape a pool worker would terminate the process, and an unset promise
  would hang the caller forever in `future::get()`.
- **The pool is persistent by design.** The first consumer is the per-request read
  path, where creating threads per batch would cost more than the overlap saves.

This commit is self-contained and adds no caller; it compiles and tests on its own.

**2. `[Store] Read a batch's LOCAL_DISK endpoints in parallel`**

Three call sites shared that serial loop — `batch_get_buffer_internal`,
`batch_get_into_internal` and `batch_get_into_multi_buffers_internal`. The grouping
and the read now go through one private helper, `RealClient::read_local_disk_endpoints`,
which returns one entry per non-empty endpoint carrying that read's status. Each site
keeps its own merge loop unchanged.

**Only the reads move off the caller thread.** Checksum verification and every write
into the result vectors stay on the caller thread, after the join. The three merge
loops therefore need no concurrency reasoning, and the diff stays confined to how the
reads are issued.

On the reader being safe to call concurrently:

- `ClientRequester::invoke_rpc` enters through an atomic `RpcDrainGuard` and blocks on
  `syncAwait` while a separate io context pool drives the RPC.
- `Client::BatchGetOffloadObject` goes through `TransferSubmitter`, which
  `stress_workload_test` already drives from many threads.
- The pinned-arena local path shares `LoadBatch` with `FileStorage::BatchGet`, which
  coro_rpc handlers already call concurrently.

Worker count comes from `MC_OFFLOAD_PARALLEL_WORKERS`, default `8`. The workers spend
their time blocked on the peer RPC rather than on CPU, and the useful upper bound is
however many peers one batch spans.

**Two behavior notes, called out so they are not a surprise in review:**

- Endpoints with an empty batch are now skipped uniformly. Two of the three sites
  already did this; the third cannot produce one, since it emplaces a key immediately
  after `try_emplace` on the endpoint.
- The failure log in `batch_get_into_internal` now names the endpoint, which the log
  order no longer implies once the reads overlap.

**3. `[Doc] Document MC_OFFLOAD_PARALLEL_WORKERS in the SSD offload guide`**

A row in the core settings table plus a short note on what the workers block on.

### Limitations / non-goals

- **A batch confined to a single endpoint gains nothing** — it takes the inline path
  and never touches the pool. The win scales with how many peers a batch spans.
- **No change to error semantics.** Per-endpoint failures land on exactly the same
  keys as before.
- The pool is per `RealClient` and sized once at construction; it is not resized at
  runtime.

title: [Store] Self-heal dangling LOCAL_DISK replicas on the read path
body:
## Description

A COMPLETE LOCAL_DISK replica whose backing file physically disappears (manual wipe, RemoveAll broadcast, disk loss) stays registered forever, and every `batch_get` against it just logs "SSD read failed" and hands back an empty buffer. #3711 already self-heals exactly this on the Put path (probe file existence, `EvictDiskReplica`, clean retry); the read path had no equivalent, which is the still-open half of #3465 and what #3884 tracks.

On a failed SSD read in `batch_get_buffer_internal`, the same heal now runs: the offload-file probe proves the backing file gone, the dangling replica is evicted master-side via `EvictDiskReplica`, and the key is retried once so a surviving replica (or a fresh re-put) can serve it instead of returning empty. When nothing survives, the master stops advertising the key and the miss surfaces honestly. The retry only ever heals distinct dead replicas, so it terminates. Checksum failures keep their existing path (the file exists, just corrupt, so no heal fires). Healthy reads are untouched; this is failure-path only.

`healDanglingLocalDiskReplica` moves from private to public in `client_service.h` so the RealClient read path can share the exact Put-side logic instead of growing a second copy.

Refs #3884, #3465, #3711.

- [x] Mooncake Store (`mooncake-store`)

Log sequence observed end to end: `SSD read failed ... FILE_OPEN_FAIL` -> `Evicted dangling LOCAL_DISK replica ... (backing file already gone)` -> `Object not found`. title: [Store] Add immutable bucket allocator for DFS replicas
body:
## Description

This PR implements the DFS immutable Bucket allocator proposed in:

- RFC: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/3641

It introduces a pluggable `GlobalAllocatorInterface` for DFS replica allocation while preserving the existing `DfsGlobalAllocator` as the default `shard` implementation.

A new `ImmutableBucketAllocator` can be selected with:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALLOCATOR=bucket
```

The Bucket allocator stores objects as aligned, append-only immutable entries in fixed-capacity Bucket files. Buckets are created on demand and reclaimed in LRU order.

The existing `DistributedFSDescriptor` wire format is unchanged. In Bucket mode, the existing `shard_idx` field carries the Bucket ID, preserving serialization compatibility.

### Main changes

#### Pluggable DFS allocator

- Extract `GlobalAllocatorInterface` as the Master-facing DFS allocation contract.
- Adapt `DfsGlobalAllocator` to implement the interface.
- Keep `shard` as the default allocator with unchanged behavior.
- Add configuration parsing and validation for `shard` and `bucket`.

#### Immutable Bucket allocation

- Create fixed-capacity Bucket files on demand.
- Store values as aligned, append-only entries:

  ```text
  [value bytes][zero alignment padding]
  ```

- Track entries through `PENDING`, `COMMITTED`, and `TOMBSTONE` states.
- Never overwrite entries or reuse tombstoned or rolled-back ranges.
- Assign monotonically increasing Bucket IDs.
- Allow ordered batch allocation across multiple Buckets.
- Roll back all reservations if any allocation in a batch fails.
- Match complete descriptors when committing, freeing, or updating entries.
- Seal full Buckets and create new ones up to the configured limit.

#### Bucket-level LRU eviction

- Track access and reclaim complete Buckets in LRU order.
- Exclude the active Bucket and Buckets containing pending or protected entries.
- Lock affected metadata shards in a stable order and validate every live entry against its exact DFS descriptor.
- Abort the entire eviction if any entry is processing, leased, pinned, or otherwise invalid.
- Remove replicas from metadata before deleting the Bucket file. Failed file deletion keeps the Bucket charged against capacity for a later retry.
- Trigger reclamation at configured watermarks and when allocation is exhausted.

#### Synchronous buffered Bucket I/O

- Extend the filesystem adapter to open existing files without creating them.
- Use synchronous buffered positional I/O with short-lived descriptors for Bucket requests, while retaining cached descriptors for shard files.
- Handle interrupted and partial POSIX operations, treating zero progress, premature EOF, and incomplete transfers as errors.
- Validate Bucket paths, IDs, descriptor alignment, object sizes, and ranges before I/O.
- Never create a file implicitly for an invalid or missing Bucket descriptor.

#### Master and Client integration

- Select the configured allocator during Master initialization and allocate DFS replicas through the common interface.
- Keep Bucket entries pending while replicas are `PROCESSING`, then commit them in `PutEnd` before publication.
- Tombstone reservations when writes are revoked, removed, or replaced.
- Keep DFS writes synchronous and revoke failed writes so incomplete data is never published.
- Attempt one validated whole-Bucket eviction when Bucket capacity is exhausted.
- Preserve existing shard expansion and eviction behavior in `shard` mode.

#### Configuration

The following settings are introduced:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALLOCATOR=shard | bucket
MOONCAKE_DFS_BUCKET_CAPACITY=1073741824
MOONCAKE_DFS_MAX_BUCKET_COUNT=64
```

The existing DFS settings continue to configure common filesystem and eviction behavior:

```bash
MOONCAKE_DFS_ROOT_DIR
MOONCAKE_DFS_FS_ADAPTER
MOONCAKE_DFS_ALIGNMENT
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_ENABLED
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_HIGH_WATERMARK
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_LOW_WATERMARK
MOONCAKE_DFS_EVICTION_CHECK_INTERVAL
```

`MOONCAKE_DFS_BUCKET_CAPACITY` must be nonzero, aligned to `MOONCAKE_DFS_ALIGNMENT`, and representable by the filesystem interface. `MOONCAKE_DFS_MAX_BUCKET_COUNT` must be positive.

#### Documentation

- Document the immutable Bucket layout and lifecycle.
- Document allocator selection and Bucket-specific environment variables.
- Describe allocation, rollback, commit, and whole-Bucket eviction.
- Document current operational and recovery limitations.

### Compatibility

- `shard` remains the default allocator with unchanged allocation, eviction, and I/O behavior.
- `DistributedFSDescriptor` serialization remains unchanged, so existing clients can continue using shard descriptors without configuration changes.
- Bucket capacity settings affect only `bucket` mode.
- Shard count and capacity settings do not control Bucket allocation.
